### FrameFieldParameters { #polyvector-kt-framefieldparameters }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FrameFieldParameters</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">inkThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">90.0</span> <span class="p">/</span> <span class="mf">255.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">regularizer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">smoothness</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">50.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">repairPasses</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/geometry/vectorize/polyvector/Polyvector/#L52)

Controls for building the frame field. [`inkThreshold`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt--framefieldparameters--inkthreshold) is the evidence level (0..1) above which a pixel counts as ink. [`regularizer`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt--framefieldparameters--regularizer) pushes the two directions towards a right angle (larger gives sharper junctions, smaller follows narrow junctions more closely). [`smoothness`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt--framefieldparameters--smoothness) trades fidelity to the image's local direction for smoothness; raise it only for very noisy input. [`repairPasses`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt--framefieldparameters--repairpasses) fill single-pixel holes in the ink mask. The defaults are the authors'.

Controls for tracing curves on a field. ### PolyvectorField { #polyvector-kt-polyvectorfield }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">PolyvectorField</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">evidence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FrameFieldParameters</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/geometry/vectorize/polyvector/Polyvector/#L81)

The polyvector field of a line drawing: at every ink pixel, two unsigned directions that the lines through that pixel follow. Where one stroke runs, the two directions are the stroke's direction and one across it; where strokes cross, they are the two strokes' directions. Building the field is the expensive step; [`trace`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt--polyvectorfield--trace) reads curves off it, and can be called again with different [`TraceParameters`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt-traceparameters) without rebuilding.

## PolyvectorNative.kt { #polyvectornative-kt }

Finding `field_polyvector` on this machine, and calling into it once found.

[`PolyvectorLibrary`](graphics.md#polyvectornative-kt-polyvectorlibrary) is the half that answers without loading anything: the library's file name on
this OS, the paths it is looked for in, whether one of them exists, and the Gradle task and
per-OS shell commands that build it. Its Windows list is empty, which is how a
[`NativeGeometryCapability`](graphics.md#nativegeometry-kt-nativegeometrycapability) says the build does not cover that OS yet, so the welcome page's
Geometry extensions panel offers no install route there. The path is resolved afresh on every
read, so a library built during a live session is picked up by the next box run.

The other half, internal to the package, binds the C ABI declared in
`native/field-polyvector/src/field_polyvector.h` with java.lang.foreign: one lazy downcall handle
per `fpv_` entry point, two parameter structs laid out by hand with their padding (one for the
field fit, one for the trace, following the split in [`FrameFieldParameters`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt-framefieldparameters) and
[`TraceParameters`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt-traceparameters)), and a 512-byte buffer that the field fit and the trace carry down and read a
message out of when either reports failure. The read-outs take no error buffer. The first symbol
lookup checks `fpv_abi_version` against the version this binding expects and refuses a library
that disagrees, naming the task that rebuilds it.

Reading a result copies it out of native memory into Kotlin arrays: the ink mask, the per-pixel
weight, the two directions and the singularities as one snapshot of the field, the streamlines
and the final curves as polylines, and the field and trace milliseconds the library times for
itself.

[`Polyvector`](graphics.md#polyvector-kt-polyvector) is the API over it, and its only caller.

## PolyvectorRequiredGraph.kt { #polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt }

Polyvector tracing under a graph the result has to reproduce: a [`Polyvector.vectorize`](graphics.md#polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt--vectorize) overload
that takes the curves the trace must keep, and a [`RequiredGraphDrawing`](graphics.md#polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt-requiredgraphdrawing) saying which of them it
kept.

The required graph is evidence rather than a hard constraint. Its curves are drawn into the field
the tracer fits, so strokes follow them; traced ends landing within the snap tolerance of a
required node are then moved onto that node and take its id, and a required node no traced end
reached adopts a nearby traced junction instead. A connection can still be lost, which is what
[`RequiredGraphDrawing.missingCurves`](graphics.md#polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt--requiredgraphdrawing--missingcurves) and [`RequiredGraphDrawing.missingNodes`](graphics.md#polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt--requiredgraphdrawing--missingnodes) report and
[`RequiredGraphDrawing.satisfied`](graphics.md#polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt--requiredgraphdrawing--satisfied) answers in one call.

The graph usually comes from another reading of the same image, a Morse–Smale complex's network
say, so that the traced curves share its nodes and their ids.

[`network`](graphics.md#polyvectorrequiredgraph-kt--requiredgraphdrawing--network) is the traced curves with every end within the snap tolerance of a required node moved onto that node and given its id; other shared ends become new nodes, numbered after the required ones. ## Colormaps.kt { #colormaps-kt }

The colour vocabulary the visualization helpers share: [`Color4`](graphics.md#colormaps-kt-color4), a `[0,1]`-component colour value
with no dependencies, and [`Colormaps`](graphics.md#colormaps-kt-colormaps), eight named ramps that can be sampled at any parameter.

A ramp here is a short table of evenly-spaced control points rather than a 256-entry lookup table
(nine colours for each of the matplotlib maps, seventeen for turbo, three for the house
cyan→orange), and [`Colormaps.sampleStops`](graphics.md#colormaps-kt--colormaps--samplestops) interpolates linearly between them. A caller that
colours one pixel at a time builds its own table from that: `showHeatmap` quantises the ramp into
1024 entries once per image rather than interpolating per pixel.

Names are matched after trimming and lowercasing, `gray`, `greys` and `cyan-orange` are aliases,
and an unknown name raises with [`Colormaps.names`](graphics.md#colormaps-kt--colormaps--names) in the message rather than falling back to a
default. RectSL's `colormap` and `cmap` words, `showHeatmap` and the imaging visualizers all take
that same vocabulary, so a ramp named in one place is the same ramp in another.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/color/Colormaps.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/color/Colormaps/)

### Colormaps { #colormaps-kt-colormaps }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Colormaps</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/color/Colormaps/#L89)

Perceptually-uniform colormaps as named colour ramps — matplotlib's viridis / magma / plasma / inferno, Google's turbo, Kenneth Moreland's coolwarm diverging map, and a plain grayscale. Each map is a table of evenly-spaced RGB control points taken from the published data (the viridisLite 9-class swatches for the matplotlib family, the turbo_srgb_floats LUT sampled every 16th entry, Moreland's cool→warm table); [`sampleStops`](graphics.md#colormaps-kt--colormaps--samplestops) interpolates linearly between them. This is reusable domain code — the single source of truth for the [`showHeatmap`](visualization.md#heatmap-kt--showheatmap) visualizer and RectSL's `colormap`/`cmap`, `bars`, `heat`, and `scatter` words, and directly callable from Kotlin.

## colors.kt { #colors-kt }

Colour constructors for the stdlib. Everything here returns a `Vec4` of sRGB-encoded components
clamped to `[0,1]` with alpha last, so the results drop straight into FLine colours and uniforms.

[`rgb`](graphics.md#colors-kt--rgb) / [`rgba`](graphics.md#colors-kt--rgba) accept either 0..1 or 0..255 components — the scale is inferred per call from
whether any component exceeds 1 — and [`rgb255`](graphics.md#colors-kt--rgb255) forces the 0..255 reading. [`hsl`](graphics.md#colors-kt--hsl) is HSL with the
usual cube geometry, but the result is encoded through the sRGB transfer function on the way out,
so it is *not* interchangeable with CSS `hsl()` — see [`hsl`](graphics.md#colors-kt--hsl) for what that costs. [`okhsl`](graphics.md#colors-kt--okhsl) and
[`okhsv`](graphics.md#colors-kt--okhsv) are the Oklab-based equivalents; of the two only [`okhsl`](graphics.md#colors-kt--okhsl) holds perceived lightness steady
across hue, because [`okhsv`](graphics.md#colors-kt--okhsv) scales `v` against the per-hue gamut cusp exactly as HSV always has.
Hue may be given as a fraction of a turn or in degrees (magnitude above 1 is divided
by 360) and is wrapped either way.

For sets: [`hueSetHsl`](graphics.md#colors-kt--huesethsl), [`hueSetOkhsl`](graphics.md#colors-kt--huesetokhsl) and [`hueSetOkhsv`](graphics.md#colors-kt--huesetokhsv) (aliased [`hslSet`](graphics.md#colors-kt--hslset), [`okhslSet`](graphics.md#colors-kt--okhslset), [`okhsvSet`](graphics.md#colors-kt--okhsvset))
space equally-separated hues around the wheel at a fixed saturation and lightness.
[`paletteForBackground`](graphics.md#colors-kt--paletteforbackground) starts from the same okhsl ring but then walks each entry's lightness up
or down until it clears a minimum WCAG contrast ratio against the supplied background, returning
the highest-contrast candidate it found when it cannot reach the target.

## pointing.kt { #pointing-kt }

Turning a place a person is looking at back into a place in the world.

This file does one step of that: **pixel → ray**, the unprojection that gets you from a mouse
position, a controller pose or a headset's aim to a line in the scene. [`PickScene`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt-pickscene) is the next
step, ray → named part, and [`Pointer`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt-pointer) the step before, person → pixel-or-pose. Once you have the
ray, `MeshBvh.raycast`, `intersectRayTriangle` and `intersectRayPlane` answer what it hits.

### The two camera models

Field has two unrelated camera models, and confusing them is the main hazard here:

 - **[`MeshView`](graphics.md#mesh-field-kt-meshview)** — the orbital camera behind [`TriMesh.renderPng`](graphics.md#mesh-field-kt--renderpng), Field's CPU rasterizer. Yaw,
   pitch, a distance *in multiples of the mesh's own bounding-sphere radius*, and a field of view.
   This is the one that makes pixels with no GPU, no window and no AWT, so it is the one a headless
   test or a docs capture can prove things with. [`MeshView.rayCamera`](graphics.md#pointing-kt--raycamera) inverts it, and does so by
   calling straight into [`VisionGeometryPreview.ViewFrame`](graphics.md#visiongeometrypreview-kt--visiongeometrypreview--viewframe) — *the same object the rasterizer
   projects with*, so the unprojection is the renderer's inverse by construction rather than by
   transcription.
 - **[`afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera)** — the live Vulkan scene's camera: a `lookAt` model-view and a
   [`afield.graphics.vulkan.util.SuperProjection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-superprojection), which can be a perspective frustum, an off-centre one, an
   orthographic prism, or a Lie-group interpolation *between* perspective and ortho. There is no
   closed-form frustum to re-derive for that last case, so [`rayCameraFor`](graphics.md#pointing-kt--raycamerafor) handles all of them the
   same way: it inverts the clip matrix numerically, in double precision.

### Conventions

 - **Pixel coordinates run from the top-left of the frame, y downward**, which is what GLFW's
   cursor reports (`Window.cursor` is `glfwGetCursorPos`) and what an image's rows are indexed by.
   Pixel *centres* are at half-integers: pixel `(0, 0)` covers `[0,1) x [0,1)` and its centre is
   `(0.5, 0.5)`. All the `rayThroughPixel` overloads take the pixel *index* and aim at its centre.
 - **Field's clip space is Vulkan's depth range, `z` in `0..1`**, and `y` is *up* in NDC despite
   Vulkan's default being down — [`afield.graphics.vulkan.Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer) flips it with a negative-height viewport
   (`setViewportAndScissor` sets `y = rect.y + rect.h` and `height = -rect.h`), precisely so that
   the familiar GL-style projection matrices keep working. So NDC `y = +1` is the **top** row.
 - **A ray's direction is unit length**, so [`RayCamera`](graphics.md#pointing-kt-raycamera) hit distances are in world units and
   comparable between pointers.

### Typical use

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val mesh = icosphereMesh(2)
val view = MeshView(yawDegrees = 30.0, pitchDegrees = 20.0)
val camera = view.rayCamera(mesh)
val hit = mesh.bvh().raycast(camera.rayThroughPixel(360, 270))
println(hit)                                  // the triangle under the middle of the picture
```

## pointing_pick.kt { #pointing-pick-kt }

A scene you can point at, and a hit record that names the **part** you touched rather than the
triangle.

### Why a triangle index is not an answer

`MeshBvh.raycast` returns a [`RayHit`](graphics.md#mesh-measure-kt-rayhit), and `RayHit.triangle` is an index into an [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh)'s
`indices` array. That is the right thing for a physics query and the wrong thing for a person: a
human pointing at a house wants to hear *"the east wall"*, not *"triangle 4471"*, and a triangle
index changes every time the geometry is rebuilt, so it cannot be written down, logged, compared
between two runs or used as a selection.

So a pickable carries [`PickParts`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt-pickparts) — a per-triangle part id with names — and a [`PickHit`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt-pickhit) reports
the part. Three things then become possible that were not: naming the thing you touched, keeping
a selection across a re-render, and asking whether two pointers found *the same* part.

### Where a part id comes from

In descending order of how much it is worth trusting:

 1. **The geometry already knows.** `PickParts.fromTriangulated` reads
    [`TriangulatedGeometry.sourceFace`](polytopes.md#fieldadapters-kt--triangulatedgeometry--sourceface) — the polytope layer has recorded, for every triangle it
    emits, the polygonal face it was cut from — well covered by the polytope tests and, until now,
    read by nothing in `jvmMain` outside `polytope` itself. This is the only
    source here where the id means something *outside* the mesh: it is an
    [`afield.geometry.polytope.ElementId`](polytopes.md#topology-kt-elementid) in the polytope's own topology, so it survives
    re-triangulation with a different triangulator and can be handed back to the polytope API.
 2. **The author said so.** `PickParts.of` takes the array, for a builder that knows which
    triangles it just appended — see [`TriMeshBuilder.groups`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt--groups), which records it for you.
 3. **The topology can guess.** `PickParts.byComponent` splits on connected components. Cheap and
    cheap, and exactly as good as the mesh's connectivity: a house whose walls all share vertices
    is one component and therefore one part, which is a real limitation and not a bug here.

#### What happens when the geometry is rebuilt

[`PickParts`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt-pickparts) is **keyed by triangle index and valid only for the mesh it was built from.**
[`Pickable`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt-pickable) checks the triangle count on construction, which catches the gross case; it cannot
catch a mesh of the same size with different triangles, and does not pretend to. If you rebuild
geometry every frame, rebuild the [`PickParts`](graphics.md#pointing-pick-kt-pickparts) with it and carry the *part id* — never the triangle
— across the rebuild. That is the whole reason ids exist.

### Typical use

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val floor = planeMesh(width = 4.0, height = 4.0)
val scene = pickScene {
    add("floor", floor, parts = PickParts.single(floor, "floor"))
    add("lamp", icosphereMesh(2), at = Matrix4f().translation(0f, 1.5f, 0f))
}
val camera = MeshView().rayCamera(scene.mergedMesh())
val hit = scene.pick(camera.rayThroughPixel(360, 270))
println(hit?.describe())      // "lamp / lamp  tri 812  1.8300 away  at (0.3100, 1.7200, 0.4400)"
```

## pointing_pointer.kt { #pointing-pointer-kt }

A person pointing — mouse, XR controller or pinched hand — behind one interface, and the
hover / press / drag / release machine that turns a stream of samples into an interaction.

### A pointer is three things

A ray, a select value in `0..1`, and whether it exists at all ([`PointerState`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt-pointerstate)). That is enough to
unify every pointing device Field can see:

 - **A mouse** has a ray only because a camera can be inverted ([`mousePointer`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--mousepointer)), a select value
   that is `0` or `1`, and is always active while the window has a cursor.
 - **An XR controller** has a pose and a trigger, and reports `active` when the runtime is tracking
   it ([`controllerPointer`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--controllerpointer)).
 - **A pinched hand** has 26 joints and a geometric pinch strength, read off
   [`afield.graphics.vulkan.targets.OpenXRHmdTarget`](graphics.md#openxrhmdtarget-kt-openxrhmdtarget)'s `handState`. Its select value is continuous and noisy,
   which is what the second half of this file is about ([`pinchPointer`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--pinchpointer)).

### Hysteresis, in two places

Feed raw nearest-hit results to a UI and it flickers. There are two flickers here and
[`PointerInteraction`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt-pointerinteraction) treats them separately:

 1. **The part flickers** when the ray lands near an edge two parts share, or grazes a silhouette.
   A pixel's worth of hand tremor alternates the answer every frame, and a label that alternates
   every frame is unreadable. The fix is a **dwell** guarding every transition *away* from a held
   hover — see [`PointerInteraction.switchSamples`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--pointerinteraction--switchsamples) and the rule stated on `resolveHover`. Acquiring
   a hover is never delayed, because a lag between pointing at something and it lighting up reads
   as the pointer being broken.
 2. **The click flickers** when a continuous select value sits on the threshold — which a
   geometric `pinchStrength` derived from a 40 mm range of finger separation does constantly. The
   fix is a **Schmitt trigger**: press at [`PointerInteraction.pressThreshold`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--pointerinteraction--pressthreshold), release at the lower
   [`PointerInteraction.releaseThreshold`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--pointerinteraction--releasethreshold). A value wobbling between them holds its state.

And once pressed, **the drag belongs to what it grabbed**: hover is frozen, and
[`PointerInteraction.dragOffset`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt--pointerinteraction--dragoffset) reports where the ray now crosses the plane through the original
contact point, so letting the pointer wander off the object does not drop the drag.

### Typical use

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val scene = pickScene { add("model", mesh, parts = builder.groups()) }
val pointer = mousePointer(camera = { view.rayCamera(mesh) }, cursor = { window.cursor },
                           selecting = { window.isMouseButtonPressed(GLFW_MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT) })
val interaction = PointerInteraction(scene)
forever {
    interaction.update(pointer.sample())
    if (interaction.justPressed) println("grabbed ${interaction.grabbed?.partName}")
}
```

## PaintCanvas.kt { #paintcanvas-kt }

[`PaintCanvas`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt-paintcanvas), a simulated oil-painting canvas that [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline)s are painted and drawn onto, with
its statistics ([`PaintStats`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt-paintstats), [`PaperInfo`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt-paperinfo)) and [`pngRow`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--pngrow) for showing several canvases side by side.

The canvas runs on the optional native wrapper `native/field-paint`; see [`PaintCanvas`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt-paintcanvas) for
building it. Tests: `PaintCanvasTest`, `GesturePaintReplayTest`, `StereoTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/PaintCanvas.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintCanvas/)

**Used in:** [Watercolour and ink](../watercolor.md)

Each drop comes off one hair with that hair's paint, so a double-loaded brush spatters both colours. Returns how many droplets landed. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">knife</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">line</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">knife</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintKnife</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">pressure</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ClosedFloatingPointRange</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.6..0.6</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">angle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lay</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">lift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintCanvas</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintCanvas/#L293) | Pull `knife` along every subpath of `line`, pressed `pressure` from start to end, the blade across the path or at `angle` (radians). The flexible blade rests on the high points of the dry surface and stands off them by a gap that closes as it is pressed (a light touch rides about 0.3 mm up). Wet paint above the blade is cut into its bead, or pressed out past its ends into ridges; with `lay`, below it the bead fills the surface to the blade's level: a flat-topped slab, or paint on the peaks of dry impasto only. When the blade lifts, `lift` of the bead stays where it was. |

end, or a profile at evenly spaced stations), sampled every `spacing` canvas units. The handle is tilted `tilt` degrees from upright; with `lean` it leans toward where it is going (the hairs trailing behind, as a brush is pulled), and a flat's wide axis is held across the path unless `roll` (degrees) fixes it. Where the path doubles back on itself by more than 120°, as in scrubbing, the handle keeps its lean and the brush is pushed back. |

canvas's FLine coordinates. Lengths, speed and the pressure profile are the world's, measured along the line in 3D at `mmPerWorld` mm to a world unit: each sample carries its world arc (`TimedGesture.Sample.s`), so the two eyes' gestures press, pause and run out at the same places along the line however foreshortened each sees it. Each subpath is one movement of the hand (`gap` seconds apart); straight segments are sampled every `spacing` world units, curves finely enough to follow. The handle's `tilt`, `lean` and `roll` are as in [`gesture`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--gesture), its heading taken on this canvas. |

## PaintNoise.kt { #paintnoise-kt }

Smooth 1D noise that varies a stroke along its length, the same for the same seed, so the
two eyes of a stereo pair can share it: [`PaintNoise`](graphics.md#paintnoise-kt-paintnoise).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/PaintNoise.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintNoise/)

### PaintNoise { #paintnoise-kt-paintnoise }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">PaintNoise</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintNoise/#L17)

Smooth noise for varying a stroke along itself ([`PaintCanvas.stroke`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--stroke)'s varied behaviours): a value from -1 to 1 that wanders as a stroke goes. Keyed on how far along a movement in the world a sample is (`TimedGesture.Sample.s`, mm), it lies at the same places along that movement on both canvases of a stereo pair, however long each sees it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="paintnoise-kt--paintnoise--along"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">along</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mm</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">scaleMm</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">octaves</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintNoise/#L22) | Smooth noise at `mm` along a stroke, -1..1, wandering over about `scaleMm` (a few octaves, each half the last's scale and strength), the same for the same `seed`. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">along</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">sample</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">TimedGesture</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Sample</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">scaleMm</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">octaves</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintNoise/#L32) | [`along`](graphics.md#paintnoise-kt--paintnoise--along) at a gesture's sample: by its world length, or its time where it has none. |

## PaintTools.kt { #painttools-kt }

The tools and materials a [`PaintCanvas`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt-paintcanvas) is worked with: grounds, brushes, knives, rags, pencils,
and tubes of paint.

A tool is made by its canvas ([`PaintCanvas.brush`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--brush), [`PaintCanvas.knife`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--knife), [`PaintCanvas.rag`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--rag),
[`PaintCanvas.pencil`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--pencil), [`PaintCanvas.waterBrush`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--waterbrush), [`PaintCanvas.dynamicBrush`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--dynamicbrush)) and the native ones
are `AutoCloseable`. [`BrushKind`](graphics.md#painttools-kt-brushkind) and [`BrushConfig`](graphics.md#painttools-kt-brushconfig) shape a bristle brush, [`Handling`](graphics.md#painttools-kt-handling) says how it
is moved, and [`Tubes`](graphics.md#painttools-kt-tubes) names ready-mixed colours to load it with. Tests: `PaintToolsTest`,
`DynamicBrushTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/)

**Used in:** [Paint and pencil from FLines](../paint_canvas.md), [Drawn Strokes Become Paint](../chain_drawn_paint.md), [Brushes with moving hairs](../paint_gestures.md)

### PaintLight { #painttools-kt-paintlight }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PaintLight</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">azimuth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">135.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">elevation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">25.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">strength</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L136)

A light to look at the canvas under ([`PaintCanvas.render`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--render) `light =`): from `azimuth` degrees (0 from the right, 90 from the top, 135 the upper left) at `elevation` degrees above the canvas. Relief casts shadows along it, and wet paint has an oily sheen. [`strength`](graphics.md#painttools-kt--tube--strength) scales the shading.

### PaintKnife { #painttools-kt-paintknife }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">PaintKnife</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L340)

A painting knife: a flexible steel blade `width` canvas units long, and the bead of paint it carries. It lays paint in flat slabs with ridges where it is pressed out at the blade's ends and a bead where it lifts; pressed hard without paint it scrapes the wet paint off down to the dry surface. On engine 5 a slab tears where it parts from the blade. Get one from [`PaintCanvas.knife`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--knife).

### PaintRag { #painttools-kt-paintrag }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">PaintRag</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L384)

A soft cotton rag bunched into a pad [width](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--rag) canvas units across, wiped or pressed over open paint to lift it ([`PaintCanvas.wipe`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--wipe), [`PaintCanvas.blot`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--blot)). What it lifts soaks into the cloth: the face in use loads up and lifts less until it is refolded ([`PaintCanvas.refold`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--refold)); dampened with spirits ([`PaintCanvas.dampen`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--dampen)) it lifts nearly to the ground. Only wet paint comes away: past its gel point paint is part of the dry picture.

### WaterBrush { #painttools-kt-waterbrush }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">WaterBrush</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L405)

A round watercolour brush: a belly that holds water, and the pigment dissolved in it. Where it touches the paper water flows between them by capillary suction, from the wetter to the drier: a full brush lays water and pigment, a damp one on a wet wash drinks it back up (with the pigment floating in it). A fast stroke lays less than a slow one. A light, nearly dry brush reaches only the peaks of the paper's tooth: drybrush comes from the paper, not a texture. Get one from [`PaintCanvas.waterBrush`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--waterbrush).

### DynamicBrush { #painttools-kt-dynamicbrush }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DynamicBrush</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">BrushKind</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L449)

A brush whose hairs move: a few dozen guide hairs simulated as chains of segments under a timed gesture of the handle ([`TimedGesture`](graphics.md#timedgesture-kt-timedgesture): position, pressure, tilt, lean and roll). The hairs bend against the paper and its paint, stick and slip by friction, clump when wet, and keep a bend they were forced past (retained deformation, so a brush once splayed stays splayed for a while). Load it with oil (`load`: upstream's bristles, following the hairs, carry and lay the paint) or with watercolour ([`loadWater`](graphics.md#painttools-kt--dynamicbrush--loadwater)). Get one from [`PaintCanvas.dynamicBrush`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--dynamicbrush).

class="nc">DynamicBrush</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L491) | How the hairs behave; `null` keeps a value. `friction` is static to kinetic against the surface; a joint bent more than `yieldDegrees` from its rest angle keeps some of the bend, at `plasticity` per second; rest bends straighten again at `recovery` per second; `cohesion` is how strongly the liquid in a wet brush draws its hairs together: 1 draws a full brush's tips to a point, more pulls harder and closer, 0 none, and below 0 pushes nearby hairs apart. |

## TimedGesture.kt { #timedgesture-kt }

A hand movement sampled in time, with pressure and pen orientation, which drives a brush:
[`TimedGesture`](graphics.md#timedgesture-kt-timedgesture) and its [`TimedGesture.Sample`](graphics.md#timedgesture-kt--timedgesture--sample).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/TimedGesture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/TimedGesture/)

### TimedGesture { #timedgesture-kt-timedgesture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">TimedGesture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Sample</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/TimedGesture/#L20)

A movement of the hand in time: where the tool is, when, how hard it presses, and how the handle is held. An [`afield.geometry.path.FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline) gives only a path; flicking, dragging slowly, pausing, pressing and lifting need the time and the orientation too. `PaintCanvas.gesture` makes one from an FLine at a speed; a pen or an agent can give the samples themselves.

## WaterMedia.kt { #watermedia-kt }

Watercolour and ink on paper: the [`Paper`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt-paper) kinds, [`WaterPigment`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt-waterpigment)s and their [`Watercolors`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt-watercolors)
palette, the [`WaterPaint`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt-waterpaint) mixed from them, and the reports and ledgers a wash returns.

A sheet is made with [`PaintCanvas.paper`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--paper) and worked with [`PaintCanvas.waterBrush`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--waterbrush). [`WaterMap`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt-watermap)
names the fields of the sheet's state that can be read back. Test: `WaterMediaTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia/)

**Used in:** [Watercolour and ink](../watercolor.md), [Brushes with moving hairs](../paint_gestures.md)

### Paper { #watermedia-kt-paper }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Paper</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia/#L21)

A sheet of paper for watercolour and ink ([`PaintCanvas.paper`](graphics.md#paintcanvas-kt--paintcanvas--paper)). Each is a physical make-up — how much water it holds, how fast it drinks and wicks, its grain, tooth and sizing — not a texture: the same drop behaves differently on each because the water does. The numbers are estimates in the ranges reported for each kind of paper.

Constants: `ColdPress`, `HotPress`, `Rough`, `Xuan`, `Blotting`.

### WaterPigment { #watermedia-kt-waterpigment }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">WaterPigment</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">k</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">s</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">density</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">diameterUm</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia/#L48)

A pigment as water carries it: its optics (Kubelka–Munk absorption [`k`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--k) per channel and scattering [`s`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--s), per µg/mm² of pigment) and what decides how it moves — particle [`density`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--density) (g/cm³) and [`diameterUm`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--diameterum) (dense, coarse pigment settles out onto the paper within a minute; fine pigment stays suspended), [`stain`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--stain) (per second it adsorbs onto fibres from water in the sheet, after which it can't be lifted) and [`lift`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--lift) (per second a deposit goes back into still water standing on it; a moving brush lifts much faster).

[`Watercolors`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt-watercolors) uses the common name, and `WaterPigment.of` takes any. |

With [`diameterUm`](graphics.md#watermedia-kt--waterpigment--diameterum), this is what decides how fast it settles. |

Dense, coarse pigment settles onto the paper within a minute; fine pigment stays suspended and travels with the water. |

A moving brush lifts much faster than this. |

## gestureReplay.kt { #gesturereplay-kt }

Gesture pad to brush: a take recorded on a `gesture(...)` pad, or its x and y keyframe lanes after
editing, painted onto a canvas as a [`TimedGesture`](graphics.md#timedgesture-kt-timedgesture). The pad's square is laid over a rectangle of
the canvas and the take's own timing is kept, so how fast the hand moved is how fast the brush
moves.

A pad carries pressure, tilt and twist only when it was made with `pen = true`, and only where the
pointer reported them: a mouse reports a flat 0.5 pressure while down and nothing else, and a
dimension that never left its resting value reads as unrecorded. Each one missing is filled the
way `PaintCanvas.gesture(line, …)` fills it from a path, which is to say a steady press, a steady
lean toward where the stroke is going, and a flat held across its path.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/gestureReplay.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/gestureReplay/)

## AccelerationStructure.kt { #accelerationstructure-kt }

Vulkan ray-tracing acceleration structures: [`AccelerationStructure`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt-accelerationstructure) builds a bottom-level structure
from triangles or AABBs, or a top-level one from [`RayTracingInstance`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt-raytracinginstance)s, on the [`Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer) found
from context.

Geometry is described by [`AccelerationStructureTriangles`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt-accelerationstructuretriangles) and [`AccelerationStructureAabbs`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt-accelerationstructureaabbs);
[`identityTransform3x4`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt--identitytransform3x4) is the default instance transform. After a build,
[`accelerationStructureBuildBarrier`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt--accelerationstructurebuildbarrier) makes it visible to later commands that read it, and
[`rayTracingMemoryBarrier`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt--raytracingmemorybarrier) orders ray-tracing shader writes before later shader reads.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/AccelerationStructure.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/AccelerationStructure/)

**Used in:** [Ray Tracing Examples](../ray_tracing_examples.md), [Compute your ray-traced geometry](../computed_ray_geometry.md)

## ClusterGeometry.kt { #clustergeometry-kt }

Builds NVIDIA cluster acceleration structures from compute-shader output: [`ClusterGeometry`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometry) validates [`TriangleCluster`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt-trianglecluster) records, builds cluster-level acceleration structures and one cluster BLAS for ray tracing.

It requires `VK_NV_cluster_acceleration_structure`; [`ClusterGeometryInput`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometryinput) names the producer buffers it reads.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/)

**Used in:** [Compute your ray-traced geometry](../computed_ray_geometry.md)

### TriangleCluster { #clustergeometry-kt-trianglecluster }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">TriangleCluster</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstVertex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">vertexCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">triangleCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clusterId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">geometryId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/#L32)

One Field cluster description, eight uint32 words / 32 bytes, usable by ordinary compute shaders. Positions are vec4 (xyz in world/object units); indices are uint32 LOCAL to this cluster's vertex slice. A cluster may change counts, positions and indices on every build. IDs stay yours. Invalid GPU records become degenerate geometry and set [`ClusterGeometry.status`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt--clustergeometry--status) rather than passing unchecked addresses/counts to Vulkan. No host readback occurs during builds.

### ClusterGeometryInput { #clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometryinput }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ClusterGeometryInput</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">positions</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VulkanBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">indices</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VulkanBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clusters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VulkanBuffer</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/#L45)

Borrowed producer buffers. Keep alive through build completion; synchronize any subsequent writes. `clusters` contains [`TriangleCluster`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt-trianglecluster) records. Buffer sizes, not arbitrary user-supplied addresses, determine bounds in the GPU validation/conversion pass.

### ClusterGeometry { #clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometry }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ClusterGeometry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">capacity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">verticesPerCluster</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">128</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">trianglesPerCluster</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">128</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxGeometryId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AccelerationStructureAddress</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/#L53)

General NV Mega Geometry builder: Field compute -> validated clusters -> CLAS -> one cluster BLAS. It owns bounded build/storage/scratch resources, never producer buffers. Single graphics queue; call [`build`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt--clustergeometry--build) explicitly after a producer changes geometry. Static geometry needs only one build. Recreate to increase capacity. A rebuild changes this BLAS's bounds: rebuild the containing TLAS. Cluster BLAS has an address but no VkAccelerationStructure handle; use it in [`RayTracingInstance`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt-raytracinginstance).

## ClusterGeometryDemo.kt { #clustergeometrydemo-kt }

A computed-terrain demo of [`ClusterGeometry`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometry): a compute shader writes every patch's vertices, indices and cluster
descriptions, and a ray-tracing pass renders the resulting cluster acceleration structure.

It needs a device with `VK_NV_cluster_acceleration_structure`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometryDemo.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometryDemo/)

## ComputeMesh.kt { #computemesh-kt }

[`ComputeMesh`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt-computemesh) is a compute dispatch with its own push constants inside a [`ComputeModule`](graphics.md#computemodule-kt-computemodule); the
rest of the file is the barriers that order compute work against transfers, graphics and host
reads.

Any [`ComputeTask`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt-computetask) can be added to a module, and [`computeTask`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--computetask) wraps a lambda as one.
[`computeBarrier`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--computebarrier) and [`zeroBuffer`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--zerobuffer) are ready-made tasks; [`computeMemoryBarrier`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--computememorybarrier),
[`graphicsMemoryBarrier`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--graphicsmemorybarrier), [`transferMemoryBarrier`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--transfermemorybarrier), [`hostReadBarrier`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--hostreadbarrier) and
[`graphicsHostReadBarrier`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt--graphicshostreadbarrier) record a Vulkan synchronization-2 barrier into a command buffer.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/ComputeMesh.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ComputeMesh/)

## ComputeModule.kt { #computemodule-kt }

A compute pipeline as a renderable module: [`ComputeModule`](graphics.md#computemodule-kt-computemodule) compiles and introspects a compute
shader, owns its descriptor sets, and dispatches the [`ComputeTask`](graphics.md#computemesh-kt-computetask)s registered in its `meshes`.

Boxes hold it through a [`ComputeModulePointer`](graphics.md#computemodule-kt-computemodulepointer), which swaps in a rebuilt module when the shader
is reloaded and carries live values across the interface change.

## FourVisualizers.kt { #fourvisualizers-kt }

Inline value printers for the Vulkan graphics types, so a renderer, buffer or texture shows as a
readable table when a box prints it.

[`registerFourVisualizers`](graphics.md#fourvisualizers-kt--registerfourvisualizers) runs at each new root and registers a printer for [`Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer), [`Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera),
[`Window`](graphics.md#window-kt-window), the device and swapchain types, images and buffers, uniform [`Structure`](graphics.md#structure-kt-structure)s, the module and
module-pointer types, [`Mesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-src-jvmmain-kotlin-afield-graphics-render-mesh), render-to-texture targets, [`LoadedTexture`](graphics.md#textures-kt-loadedtexture) and [`StorageImage`](graphics.md#textures-kt-storageimage). Each
printer renders a small coloured table of the object's state: frame counter and upload bytes for a
renderer, extents and formats for images, field values for a structure. [`TexturePreviewCache`](graphics.md#fourvisualizers-kt-texturepreviewcache)
holds the downscaled previews shown beside texture values.

## GeometryAgentTools.kt { #geometryagenttools-kt }

A worked, public example of giving Field's AI its own tools — two of them, over the geometry the
loaders in [MeshFromDisk.kt](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--meshfromanyfile) read off disk.

### What this is for

`afield.ai.tools.AgentToolExtensions` is how any code outside `afield.ai.core` adds tools to AI4.
This file is the runnable half of `public/docs/aiFeatures.md`'s "Give the AI a tool of your own",
built out of parts that are useful on their own:
[`meshFromAnyFile`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--meshfromanyfile) reads OBJ, STL, PLY, glTF/GLB and everything else Assimp handles, and
[`afield.geometry.mesh.renderPng`](graphics.md#mesh-field-kt--renderpng) rasterises the result with no GPU, no window and no AWT.

That last property is what makes the second tool worth copying. A model asked "is the scan I dropped
in there the right way up?" can *look*, because [`InspectGeometryFileResult`](graphics.md#geometryagenttools-kt-inspectgeometryfileresult) implements
[`CarriesToolImages`](machine-learning.md#tools-kt-carriestoolimages) and the picture travels as an image rather than as base64 spent in a JSON string.

### Using it

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
// in a box:
GeometryAgentTools.addSearchRoot(File(System.getProperty("user.home"), "scans"))
GeometryAgentTools.register()
// then open AI Chat and ask about the files in there.
```

[`GeometryAgentTools.register`](graphics.md#geometryagenttools-kt--geometryagenttools--register) is idempotent, so leaving those two lines in a box you re-run is
fine, and a re-run reaches a conversation that is already open.

### The three things this example is trying to demonstrate

 1. **A gate on the tool set.** Both tools are unavailable until a search root is added. A tool set
    that is always on costs its schema on every request in every conversation, including the ones
    that have nothing to do with it.
 2. **A result that summarises itself.** Both results implement [`SummarisesForToolLog`](machine-learning.md#agenttoolextensions-kt-summarisesfortoollog), so the tool
    I/O log — which `AiToolUseImprovementMonitor` reads — records what happened rather than a class
    name.
 3. **Refusing to read outside the roots.** These tools take a *path from a language model*. The
    roots are the entire permission model, and `resolveInsideRoots` is where it is enforced; a
    symlink or a `../` that escapes is an error, not a read. Every tool that takes a path from a
    model needs an equivalent, and it is the part an example is most likely to leave out.

### What this does not do

It does not modify anything. There is no `ConvertGeometryFile` here: a writing tool
needs a confirmation protocol (the personal house cluster's `commit=false` preview pattern), which is
a bigger subject than one example should carry.

## Mesh.kt { #mesh-kt-src-jvmmain-kotlin-afield-graphics-render }

[`Mesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-src-jvmmain-kotlin-afield-graphics-render-mesh) is the vertex-buffer draw call of a graphics module: it holds the vertex inputs and push
constants the module's shaders declare, and draws them on the [`Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer) found from context.

Its layout has to agree with the vertex-buffer structure the module's pipeline was built with.
[`fullscreenTriangle`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-src-jvmmain-kotlin-afield-graphics-render--fullscreentriangle) makes the one-triangle mesh used for full-screen passes.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/Mesh.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/Mesh/)

**Used in:** [Field 4 Graphics](../afield_four_graphics.md), [Field Probes: instrumenting shaders](../field_probes.md), [FieldML's JVM bridge](../fieldml_host_bridge.md)

## MeshBuilder.kt { #meshbuilder-kt }

Two ways of writing vertices into a `Mesh`, of which one is wired up.

[`writeSuperMap`](graphics.md#meshbuilder-kt--writesupermap) is the live one, and it is where `m.set(4, 2) { … }` in a shader box comes from. It
reads a vertex shader's introspected inputs and returns Kotlin source: a `MappedStructure` holding
one buffer field per input, and a `Mesh.set(numVert, numTriangle)` extension that resizes the mesh
and maps all of those buffers at once, so the lambda can assign them by the names the shader itself
declares. `insertForShader` calls this whenever a `moduleHere` box's vertex and fragment shaders
compile, and appends the text to that box's preamble.

[`MeshBuilder`](graphics.md#meshbuilder-kt-meshbuilder), [`VertexData`](graphics.md#meshbuilder-kt-vertexdata) and [`writeVertexData`](graphics.md#meshbuilder-kt--writevertexdata) are the other way: stage vertex bytes on the CPU
through generated `write(...)` calls, then copy them into the mesh's buffers in one pass. `Mesh`
constructs a [`MeshBuilder`](graphics.md#meshbuilder-kt-meshbuilder) for every mesh and offers it as `builder { }`, but nothing in the tree
calls [`writeVertexData`](graphics.md#meshbuilder-kt--writevertexdata) to generate those `write` methods, and nothing calls the internal
`closeAndApply` that copies the staged bytes across, so vertices staged this way never reach the
mesh. `m.set` is the route to use.

## MeshModule.kt { #meshmodule-kt }

A task/mesh-shader pipeline as a renderable module: [`MeshModule`](graphics.md#meshmodule-kt-meshmodule) compiles and introspects task and
mesh shaders and owns their descriptor sets.

Boxes hold it through a [`MeshModulePointer`](graphics.md#meshmodule-kt-meshmodulepointer), which swaps in a rebuilt module when a shader is
reloaded and carries live values across the interface change.

## Module.kt { #module-kt }

The rasterising [`Module`](graphics.md#module-kt-module): one graphics pipeline built from vertex/fragment (or task/mesh)
GLSL, the [`Mesh`](graphics.md#module-kt--parameters--mesh-2)es it draws, and the uniforms, textures and push constants bound to it.

[`Parameters`](graphics.md#module-kt-parameters) carries the shader sources and pipeline settings, and [`parameters`](graphics.md#module-kt--parameters) builds one
against the renderer found by `fromContext()`. A [`ModulePointer`](graphics.md#module-kt-modulepointer) stands in front of a module so
a box can recompile its shaders and swap in the new [`Module`](graphics.md#module-kt-module) without the renderer losing its
reference; [`Module.pointer`](graphics.md#module-kt--pointer) makes one. [`before`](graphics.md#module-kt--before) wraps a command-buffer callback as a target
that runs ahead of the module's draws, and [`parseCompilerException`](graphics.md#module-kt--parsecompilerexception) splits a shader compiler
error into file, line and message.

Box code usually reaches this through `moduleHere` rather than constructing a [`Module`](graphics.md#module-kt-module)
directly; the graphics lessons in `public/docs/assets/canonical_graphics/LESSONS.md` show
that shape.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/Module.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/Module/)

**Used in:** [Fabricate Renderer](../fabricate_renderer.md), [FieldML's JVM bridge](../fieldml_host_bridge.md), [A solid, written down: `afield.lang.solidsl`](../solid_notation.md)

## ModuleRebuild.kt { #modulerebuild-kt }

Told when a module pointer swaps in a rebuilt module (a full shader reload), with the old and new
modules' live uniform structures, before the old one is dropped.

**Order.** The generic carry-over (`ReloadCarryOver.finish`) runs first and is authoritative: it has
already moved every value and binding that still fits the new reflection, and dropped (and reported)
the rest. Only then are [`hooks`](graphics.md#modulerebuild-kt--modulerebuild--hooks) called, with a [`Rebuild`](graphics.md#modulerebuild-kt--modulerebuild--rebuild) saying which new structures were carried and
from which old one. A hook fills in what the generic carry could not know (a `stack.auto` numbers
block with no old counterpart is seeded from its slot) and must not re-apply what was carried, or
it would restore bindings the carry dropped as retyped and values it refused. Both steps run in
`ReloadCarryOver.finishAndNotify`.

An in-place pipeline update keeps its structures and does not come here.

## RayTracingModule.kt { #raytracingmodule-kt }

The ray-tracing counterpart of [`Module`](graphics.md#module-kt-module): a Vulkan ray-tracing pipeline built from raygen,
miss, hit-group and callable shaders, with its shader binding table and bound resources.

[`RayTracingGroups`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt-raytracinggroups) lists the stages; `RayTracingGroups.fromParameters` builds it from the
single-stage sources on [`Parameters`](graphics.md#module-kt-parameters). A [`RayTracingModulePointer`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt-raytracingmodulepointer) lets a box swap a recompiled
module in place, as [`ModulePointer`](graphics.md#module-kt-modulepointer) does for rasterising modules. Work is recorded as
[`RayTracingTask`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt-raytracingtask)s: [`RayTracingDispatch`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt-raytracingdispatch) traces a width × height × depth grid of rays, and
[`rayTracingTask`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt--raytracingtask) wraps an arbitrary command-buffer callback. [`rayTracingHostReadBarrier`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt--raytracinghostreadbarrier)
makes ray-tracing shader writes visible to a host read.

## ReloadCarryOver.kt { #reloadcarryover-kt }

What survives when a module compiles a new shader and swaps it in: which uniform buffers keep
their contents, which are reallocated, which are retired, and which of the values already written
into them are re-applied.

Every module pointer finishes a reload through `ReloadCarryOver.finishAndNotify`, which runs this
generic policy first and the [`ModuleRebuild`](graphics.md#modulerebuild-kt-modulerebuild) hooks second, so a hook only fills in what the policy
left. The policy reads the [`ShaderInterfaceTransition`](graphics.md#shaderinterfacetransition-kt-shaderinterfacetransition) between the old and new introspections. A
uniform block whose layout is unchanged keeps its buffer and its bytes, including across a rename,
since the same members at the same offsets still mean what they meant. A block that was resized or
retyped gets a fresh buffer, zeroed before anything writes it, and the values set on the old one
are re-applied wherever they still fit the new reflection. A buffer the old module allocated and
the new one does not use goes through the renderer's retirement queue rather than being freed under
a frame that may still be reading it.

Only a buffer the module allocated for itself is zeroed, carried by layout or retired. One that
came from the surrounding context, or that a resolver the box supplied handed back, is resolved
again the way it was the first time and is never freed here. Zeroing applies to uniform blocks
only: a storage buffer has its values carried and is retired the same way, but its contents are
left as they are.

[`ModuleReloadReport`](graphics.md#reloadcarryover-kt-modulereloadreport) is what the box side reads back: the transition, and one note per value that
could not be carried, so a reload that silently dropped a uniform says which one.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/ReloadCarryOver.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ReloadCarryOver/)

### ModuleReloadReport { #reloadcarryover-kt-modulereloadreport }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ModuleReloadReport</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">transition</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ShaderInterfaceTransition</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">notes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyList</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ReloadCarryOver/#L50)

What a module pointer's full `reload` did to the interface: the `transition` old→new (null when the pointer could not compare, for want of an introspection) and `notes`, one per value that could not be carried to the new module. Read by the box-side reload (`reloadShader` and siblings) to say it.

## ReloadResolvers.kt { #reloadresolvers-kt }

Keeps a module's resource resolvers one layer deep across repeated shader reloads.

Each module pointer installs its carry-over behaviour by replacing the resolvers on its
[`Parameters`](graphics.md#module-kt-parameters). [`Module`](graphics.md#module-kt-module), [`ComputeModule`](graphics.md#computemodule-kt-computemodule) and [`MeshModule`](graphics.md#meshmodule-kt-meshmodule) replace all three of `uboResolver`,
`ssboResolver` and `textureResolver`; [`RayTracingModule`](graphics.md#raytracingmodule-kt-raytracingmodule) replaces the latter two. A reload is
handed a copy of the parameters, and a copy brings the resolvers across as they are, so each
wrap would otherwise land on the one the previous reload installed and every uniform, buffer and
texture lookup would walk one closure more than it did on the run before.

`reloadWrap` unwraps before it wraps, so what sits underneath stays the resolver the box or
`moduleHere` supplied and the depth stays at one however often a shader is reloaded.
`reloadWrapDepth` reports that depth; `ReloadResolversTest` holds it at one across a hundred
reloads, and checks that replacing the resolver yourself makes the replacement what the next
reload wraps.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/ReloadResolvers.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ReloadResolvers/)

## SplatCloudEdit.kt { #splatcloudedit-kt }

Editable CPU-side Gaussian splat clouds: [`SplatCloud`](graphics.md#splatcloudedit-kt-splatcloud) holds splats in world-unit scales, 0..1 opacity and linear colour, so cropping, filtering, decimating, transforming and merging are plain arithmetic.

A cloud converts from the table [`readCompressedSplatPly`](graphics.md#compressedsplatply-kt--readcompressedsplatply) reads and writes back out as a `.compressed.ply` that [`CompressedSplatPly`](graphics.md#compressedsplatply-kt-compressedsplatply) reads again.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/SplatCloudEdit.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/SplatCloudEdit/)

## SplatCloudEditTest.kt { #splatcloudedittest-kt }

Tests the splat cloud edit loop: read a compressed PLY into a [`SplatCloud`](graphics.md#splatcloudedit-kt-splatcloud), query and edit it,
preview it, and write it back with [`CompressedSplatPlyWriter`](graphics.md#compressedsplatplywriter-kt-compressedsplatplywriter).

It checks two claims that reading the code cannot settle:

1. **A cloud that goes out comes back.** [`CompressedSplatPlyWriter`](graphics.md#compressedsplatplywriter-kt-compressedsplatplywriter) is a new encoder and the only
   thing standing behind it is that it is the inverse of [`CompressedSplatPly`](graphics.md#compressedsplatply-kt-compressedsplatply)'s decoder. So: write,
   read back, and compare, with the error pinned at the digits the quantization actually delivers.
   And separately, write the *same* input through `CompressedSplatPlyFixture` — the independent
   transcription of splat-transform's own encoder that already lives here — and require the bytes
   to be identical, so the writer is checked against an encoder other than the reader it mirrors.
2. **The CPU transform is the transform the GPU bakes.** [`SplatCloud.transformed`](graphics.md#splatcloudedit-kt--splatcloud--transformed) decomposes and
   re-composes a rotation and three scales; `packInto` folds the same matrix into the covariance
   congruence and never writes it down. If those two disagree, an edited cloud looks different
   after it is saved, and no amount of float comparison inside either path would show it. So the
   test rasterizes both and compares pixels.

## SplatFusedPackTest.kt { #splatfusedpacktest-kt }

Tests [`GaussianSplatRenderer.packInto`](renderers.md#gaussiansplatrenderer-kt--gaussiansplatrenderer--packinto) — the fused compressed-file-to-GPU-layout path — against
[`GaussianSplatRenderer.pack`](renderers.md#gaussiansplatrenderer-kt--gaussiansplatrenderer--pack) over the [`PlyFloatTable`](graphics.md#loadply-kt-plyfloattable), which is the same computation the slow way.

The two are not bit-identical. The compressed format stores colour as linear 0..1 and
opacity post-sigmoid, which is exactly what the shader consumes, so the fused path skips the
`f_dc = (c - 0.5) / SH_C0` and logit round trips that the table path performs and undoes. Every
other quantity — position, scale, rotation, covariance — is computed by the same expressions in
the same order and to the same spelling, so the tolerances below are tight enough that a swapped
field or a wrong bit shift cannot pass.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/SplatFusedPackTest.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/SplatFusedPackTest/)

## SplatRasterTest.kt { #splatrastertest-kt }

Tests [`SplatRaster`](graphics.md#splatraster-kt-splatraster) at the level of pixels.

`SplatFusedPackTest` checks that the two pack paths produce the same *floats*, and every assertion
in it would still hold if the shader drew the cloud mirrored, upside down, or with red and blue
swapped. This is the test that cannot. It asserts:

- **Orientation**, from four corner-marked splats — the only proof of the Y and X conventions that
  does not reduce to re-deriving the same viewport call the rasterizer was written from.
- **A known splat at a known pixel in a known colour**, with the pixel derived on paper from the
  perspective matrix and written here as a literal, so a change in the projection has to be
  noticed rather than absorbed.
- **Slot sensitivity** — the differential oracle. Each of the sixteen floats in
  [`GaussianSplatRenderer`](renderers.md#gaussiansplatrenderer-kt-gaussiansplatrenderer)'s layout is perturbed in turn, and the image is required to move for the
  thirteen the shader reads and to *not* move for the three it does not, which tests that the CPU
  and the GPU read the same cloud.
- **Pixel agreement between the two pack paths**, which is `SplatFusedPackTest`'s float claim
  carried through to what a person actually sees.
- **That the poison detector detects poison.** A cloud is broken with NaNs and the
  non-finite count is required to find exactly them — and required to be zero on good data, so the
  detector cannot be passing by always firing.

## SplatTools.kt { #splattools-kt }

A command line over the CPU splat toolchain, for looking at a capture without opening Field.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
run-jvm-main afield.graphics.render.SplatToolsKt sheet ~/Downloads/circle-05-a120p0_00001_ out/
run-jvm-main afield.graphics.render.SplatToolsKt frame ~/Downloads/shot/frame_000060.compressed.ply out/
```

`sheet` draws a contact sheet of frames spread across a capture directory; `frame` rasterizes one
compressed PLY. Both run on the CPU through [`SplatRaster`](graphics.md#splatraster-kt-splatraster), so judging a fresh capture (is it any
good, which frames are worth looking at) needs no GPU, window or scrubbing.

## StandardDrawing.kt { #standarddrawing-kt }

The small vocabulary of `FLine` construction and styling that sketches and examples reach for
first.

[`fline`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--fline) is the builder; the [`rangeTo`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--rangeto) operator makes a one-segment line out of two vectors
(`a..b`, composable with `+=`), and the styling overloads of `moveTo` / `lineTo` / `cubicTo`
position a node and style it in the same call. Appearance is carried by delegated properties on
`FLine` and `FLine.Node` — `color`, `thickness`, `thicken`, `filled`, `stroked`, `pointed`,
`pointSize` — which the renderers read back; `onClick` and `hoverColor` only do anything in the
interactive outputs.

The rest are shape helpers: `rect` and [`Rect.toFLine`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--tofline), `arrow` (a real filled arrowhead rather
than a point sprite), [`seg`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--seg), and [`fitInto`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--fitinto), which scales and centres a list of lines into a
`Rect` using their 2D bounds only.
