### Top-level values { #standarddrawing-kt-values }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--color"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector4f</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L124) | The line's colour as RGBA in `0..1` (sRGB, alpha included) — one colour for the stroke, the fill and the node dots alike. Opaque white when never set. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector4f</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L135) | Per-node colour override in `0..1`, which is how one FLine carries a gradient: the GPU point/triangle writers in `afield.graphics.render.StandardDrawing` use a node's own colour where it has one and the whole line's [`color`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--color) where it does not. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--thickness"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">thickness</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L141) | Stroke width, in the same units as the line's own points (pixels, for the 2D outputs). `null` — the default — means "unset", which every renderer reads as 1.0 rather than as "invisible". |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--thicken"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">thicken</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Stroke</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L151) | An AWT [`Stroke`](visualization.md#strokesketch-kt-stroke) that replaces "stroke at one width" with "convert this line into the outline of its own stroke" — dashes, tapers, calligraphic pens, anything `Stroke.createStrokedShape` can do. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--filled"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">filled</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L157) | Whether closed subpaths are flooded with [`color`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--color). `false` by default, and independent of [`stroked`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--stroked) — with both true the renderers fill and then draw the outline on top. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--stroked"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">stroked</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L164) | Whether the path is stroked at [`thickness`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--thickness). `true` by default; with this and [`filled`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--filled) both false the geometry still exists and still hit-tests, but nothing is drawn except the node dots that [`pointed`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--pointed) asks for. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--pointed"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pointed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L171) | Draw a dot at every node of the line — every `moveTo`/`lineTo`/`cubicTo` endpoint, not the interior control points of a cubic and not `close`. Off by default. The fast way to see where a path's points actually landed, and how a particle set gets drawn at all. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--pointsize"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pointSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L180) | Size of the dots [`pointed`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--pointed) draws, 1.0 by default, overridable node by node with [`FLine.Node.pointSize`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--pointsize). |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pointSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L187) | Per-node override of the line's [`FLine.pointSize`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--pointsize), under the same `* 3` radius convention. `null` — the default, and unlike the line-level property this one is not written back on read — means "follow the line". |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--onclick"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">onClick</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">FLineIntersection</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">-</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L312) | Callback invoked when this FLine is clicked in an interactive output. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--label"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L321) | A human name for this line, reported back as [`FLineIntersection.label`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--flineintersection--label) when it is clicked and used as the heading by `afield.ui.visualization.inspect`. |
| <a id="standarddrawing-kt--hovercolor"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">hoverColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec4</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L327) | Color to show when the pointer hovers over this FLine in an interactive SVG output. When null no hover color change is applied. |

### FLineHitKind { #standarddrawing-kt-flinehitkind }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FLineHitKind</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L197)

What kind of thing on a figure a click landed on — the same three-way distinction the editable FLine widget already draws its hit targets with (`data-fline-hit-kind` in `sliders.js`), now reported to [`FLine.onClick`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--onclick) as well.

Constants: `POINT`, `EDGE`, `FACE`, `UNKNOWN`.

### FLineFaceCoordinates { #standarddrawing-kt-flinefacecoordinates }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FLineFaceCoordinates</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L215)

Which convention [`FLineIntersection.u`](graphics.md#standarddrawing-kt--flineintersection--u) and `v` follow for a `FLineHitKind.FACE` hit — because there is no one right answer for a face nobody chose, and a plausible wrong number is worse than a labelled one.

Constants: `NONE`, `BILINEAR`, `BOUNDING_BOX`.

## groups.kt { #groups-kt }

Mesh groups: lists of meshes that share one live push-constant binding.

[`MeshGroup`](graphics.md#groups-kt-meshgroup), [`MeshMeshGroup`](graphics.md#groups-kt-meshmeshgroup) and [`ComputeMeshGroup`](graphics.md#groups-kt-computemeshgroup) each carry a `BoundFromStructure` delegate, so
a property assigned on the group (a supplier `() -> T`) is bound to the push constant of the same
name in every member, and read back from the first member that has it. A name no member's module
declares as a push constant throws. [`bindPush`](graphics.md#groups-kt--bindpush) is the looser form for meshes that are not in a
group: it runs one binding block against each target in turn.

## DirectLighting.kt { #directlighting-kt }

Direct lighting from one-sided rectangular area emitters, shaded over a raster G-buffer.

[`DirectLighting`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlighting) is a render target that [`DirectLighting.attach`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt--directlighting--attach) adds to a render list's pre-targets.
It reads [`DirectLightSurfaces`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlightsurfaces): world position and depth, normal, albedo, the unlit source image
and motion.
It lights those surfaces from an [`AreaEmitter`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-areaemitter), tracing shadow rays against an [`OpaqueRayScene`](graphics.md#opaquerayscene-kt-opaquerayscene)
when the device supports ray queries; otherwise its mode defaults to passing the source image
through, with an unshadowed mode available.
[`DirectLighting.enableRtxdi`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt--directlighting--enablertxdi) adds optional RTXDI reservoir resampling, configured by [`RtxdiSettings`](graphics.md#rtxdisettings-kt-rtxdisettings).
The `view` setting switches the output to debug images such as normals, depth or light id.

Raster surface contract. XYZ world position + Vulkan depth [0,1] (clear=1, not reversed); XYZ world shading normal; linear RGB albedo. Motion is currentUV-previousUV, Y down, unjittered. Point sampling only. Material identity, emission, eligibility and temporal validity are NOT alpha. The optional RTXDI bridge snapshots these inputs; material IDs are not encoded in alpha.

## DirectLightingDemo.kt { #directlightingdemo-kt }

A small scene for trying [`DirectLighting`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlighting): a floor, three cubes and a moving area light.

[`DirectLightingDemo`](graphics.md#directlightingdemo-kt-directlightingdemo) builds the raster renderer, the [`OpaqueRayScene`](graphics.md#opaquerayscene-kt-opaquerayscene) and the lighting pass at a
given size; call [`DirectLightingDemo.animate`](graphics.md#directlightingdemo-kt--directlightingdemo--animate) from the box's frame loop and
[`DirectLightingDemo.moveObject`](graphics.md#directlightingdemo-kt--directlightingdemo--moveobject) to move a cube. Re-running the box that built it closes the
previous instance. [`DirectLightingSmoke`](graphics.md#directlightingdemo-kt-directlightingsmoke) is the standalone entrypoint behind the
`four.direct-lighting.smoke` smoke test, with a `--fallback` mode that runs without ray tracing.

## LightingGpuTimer.kt { #lightinggputimer-kt }

How long a lighting pass took on the GPU, timed per swapchain image.

Two timestamps per image, top of pipe to bottom, reused once the renderer has waited on that
image's fence. Each `begin` collects the previous result if it is available, so reading one never
costs a CPU wait, and the last 1024 readings stay in `samples` in milliseconds for a live box.

The queries are a slice of a pool shared with other timers (`TimestampSlabs`), not a pool of
their own: KosmicKrisp backs every `VkQueryPool` with a Metal counter heap, and a process gets
32 of those, each at most 4096 timestamps (measured, SDK 1.4.363, M1 Max), which a pool per timer
exhausts. A timer that cannot get a slice records nothing.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/lighting/LightingGpuTimer.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/lighting/LightingGpuTimer/)

## OpaqueRayScene.kt { #opaquerayscene-kt }

Opaque triangle geometry for ray-query visibility, as used by [`DirectLighting`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlighting) for shadows.

[`OpaqueTriangles`](graphics.md#opaquerayscene-kt-opaquetriangles) is an immutable indexed mesh (`OpaqueTriangles.box` makes a box), and an
[`OpaqueInstance`](graphics.md#opaquerayscene-kt-opaqueinstance) places one with a stable id and transform. [`OpaqueRayScene.commit`](graphics.md#opaquerayscene-kt--opaquerayscene--commit) takes the
instance list and builds one bottom-level acceleration structure per geometry and a new top-level
structure for each edit, waiting for the build, so commit between frames on the render thread.
`OpaqueRayScene.available` reports whether the device supports ray queries.

## RtxdiEngine.kt { #rtxdiengine-kt }

The RTXDI implementation behind [`DirectLighting`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlighting)'s two RTXDI modes: reservoir resampling run
entirely as compute passes over GPU buffers, with none of the SDK's CPU-side wrapper linked in.

An engine is built when RTXDI is enabled and sized from the render dimensions it finds then, and
it owns what that sizing implies: a packed surface buffer, host-visible buffers per swapchain
image for the camera matrices and for this frame's and the previous frame's area lights, and
reservoir storage of three slices of 24 bytes a pixel, rounded up to whole 16×16 tiles. That
allocation is checked against the device's `maxStorageBufferRange` as the engine is built, so an
oversized render resolution is refused there rather than inside a descriptor write. Ray queries
are required.

Reuse across frames holds only while the history does. Every frame compares the projection, the
camera (a view difference over 0.75 counts as a cut), the acceleration structure's build count and
a signature of the sampling settings, and any change resets the history and records which of them
it was. A reference render runs a single reference estimator in place of the four resampling
stages and leaves no history behind. The reconstruction filter that can follow runs over the
radiance view alone, and feeds neither the estimator nor the reservoirs.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/lighting/RtxdiEngine.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/lighting/RtxdiEngine/)

## RtxdiProgram.kt { #rtxdiprogram-kt }

Loads the optional RTXDI shaders, and refuses a binary whose interface disagrees with the host
code written against it.

Field does not ship NVIDIA's sampling SDK and loads nothing from it at startup. Running
`tools/lighting/build_rtxdi.py --prepare` clones the SDK and fetches a shader compiler into
ignored build storage, and the build leaves a manifest under
`build/lighting-experiment/rtxdi-shaders/`. `load` reads that manifest; with no manifest there it
fails with the command to run.

What `load` then checks is the interface rather than the file. The manifest has to record the SDK
commit this source was written against, the SPIR-V has to hash to what the manifest recorded, and
the shader's own reflection has to still carry the workgroup size, the push-constant block's size
and member offsets, the reservoir and offset array strides, and the surface and light struct
layouts that the host side writes into. Shaders rebuilt from a different SDK revision therefore
fail to load, instead of being handed the host's bytes at offsets that have moved.

A loaded program is passed to [`DirectLighting`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlighting) through `enableRtxdi`, which builds the pass and
leaves the current one in place if that fails.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/lighting/RtxdiProgram.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/lighting/RtxdiProgram/)

## RtxdiSettings.kt { #rtxdisettings-kt }

Live controls for the RTXDI resampling path of [`DirectLighting`](graphics.md#directlighting-kt-directlighting).

[`RtxdiSettings`](graphics.md#rtxdisettings-kt-rtxdisettings) holds the camera matrices, temporal and spatial reuse parameters, shadowing and an
optional spatial denoise, and takes the light list as [`IdentifiedAreaLight`](graphics.md#rtxdisettings-kt-identifiedarealight)s through
[`RtxdiSettings.commitLights`](graphics.md#rtxdisettings-kt--rtxdisettings--commitlights), so a light keeps its history across reordering. Edit it on the render
thread between frames; [`RtxdiSettings.resetHistory`](graphics.md#rtxdisettings-kt--rtxdisettings--resethistory) discards history after a cut or material edit.

## megaTextures.kt { #megatextures-kt }

A directory of images as one texture, however many of them there are.

[`Box.megaTextureHere`](graphics.md#megatextures-kt--megatexturehere) is the whole box-facing surface: point it at a folder and it scans the
folder, builds the atlas, and registers the GLSL your shaders interpolate with `{{ mega.all }}`.
The machinery behind it lives in `afield.graphics.texture.mega`, and the reason it is worth reaching
for rather than a pile of `LoadedTexture`s is that it is *GPU-driven*: the fragment shader
measures its own on-screen footprint and asks for the resolution it needs, so nothing here has to
be told where anything is or how big it looks.

`dev_docs/agents/transcripts/mega_texture_wall.yaml` is the worked example — five lines of Kotlin
and two shaders you can edit live.

## OpenDlssNrImage.kt { #opendlssnrimage-kt }

Runs one image file through [`OpenDlssNrPass`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrpass) and shows the result on screen.

[`OpenDlssNrImage`](graphics.md#opendlssnrimage-kt-opendlssnrimage) loads the image and requires [`OpenDlssNrSupport.availability`](graphics.md#opendlssnrsupport-kt--opendlssnrsupport--availability-2) to be ready. After
[`OpenDlssNrImage.install`](graphics.md#opendlssnrimage-kt--opendlssnrimage--install) it evaluates the pass each frame under the renderer, with `controls`
for the network and `exposure`, `gamma` and `offset` for grading the result as it reaches the
screen.

## OpenDlssNrPass.kt { #opendlssnrpass-kt }

The Vulkan pass that runs the native neural-rendering (NR) network over a sampled image.

[`OpenDlssNrPass.evaluate`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt--opendlssnrpass--evaluate) takes [`OpenDlssNrInputs`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrinputs) (colour with its [`OpenDlssNrColorEncoding`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrcolorencoding), and
optional motion and depth guides for temporal mode), an [`OpenDlssNrFrame`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrframe) and the current
[`OpenDlssNrControls`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrcontrols) (seed, style, tone, structure, intensity), and writes the result to its output
texture. [`OpenDlssNrPass.postEffect`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt--opendlssnrpass--posteffect) wraps it as a post effect, and [`OpenDlssNrPass.reset`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt--opendlssnrpass--reset) drops
temporal history after a cut or edit.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/neural/OpenDlssNrPass.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/neural/OpenDlssNrPass/)

**Used in:** [Neural image rendering with OpenDLSS-NR](../open_dlss_nr.md)

### OpenDlssNrColorEncoding { #opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrcolorencoding }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">OpenDlssNrColorEncoding</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/neural/OpenDlssNrPass/#L30)

What a Vulkan sampler returns. SRGB-format views already decode, so use LINEAR_LDR for those.

Constants: `SRGB_CODE`, `LINEAR_LDR`, `LINEAR_HDR`.

### OpenDlssNrControls { #opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrcontrols }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OpenDlssNrControls</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">style</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">tone</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">structure</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">skin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">autoMask</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">intensity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">temporal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/neural/OpenDlssNrPass/#L34)

Style is the network condition, independently of grading after the pass. Tone and structure take any finite binary16 value: -10..30 is useful for image exploration. Skin is active only with autoMask; negative skin inherits structure. Fixed seed is the default.

Top-left origin, same-sized sampled images. Motion is UV displacement, by default Field's current-minus-previous convention; depth is standard Vulkan depth with background 1. Temporal mode needs both guides. An arbitrary image/video must supply real motion to use history.

### OpenDlssNrPass { #opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrpass }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OpenDlssNrPass</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/neural/OpenDlssNrPass/#L60)

Optional native Vulkan pass, recorded outside render passes on Field's graphics queue. Construct/evaluate/edit/close on the renderer thread. Recreate at a new resolution; close retires behind Field's completion fences. The output is linear RGBA16F, ready for normal Field grading. No CPU frame transfer or private per-frame submit occurs. Failure is explicit; callers can use availability() before creating the pass and present the source when unavailable.

## OpenDlssNrStudy.kt { #opendlssnrstudy-kt }

An editable source image fed through the native neural-rendering (NR) pass, with a graded comparison.

[`OpenDlssNrStudy`](graphics.md#opendlssnrstudy-kt-opendlssnrstudy) renders a source, either a fragment shader, a loaded image or a small geometry
scene, into a texture, runs it through [`OpenDlssNrPass`](graphics.md#opendlssnrpass-kt-opendlssnrpass) when [`OpenDlssNrSupport`](graphics.md#opendlssnrsupport-kt-opendlssnrsupport) reports the
native library ready, and displays a graded comparison. Without the library it still shows the
source. [`OpenDlssNrStudy.reload`](graphics.md#opendlssnrstudy-kt--opendlssnrstudy--reload) swaps shaders live and [`OpenDlssNrStudy.saveFrame`](graphics.md#opendlssnrstudy-kt--opendlssnrstudy--saveframe) captures a frame.

## OpenDlssNrSupport.kt { #opendlssnrsupport-kt }

Whether the native neural-rendering (NR) pass can run on this renderer.

[`OpenDlssNrSupport.availability`](graphics.md#opendlssnrsupport-kt--opendlssnrsupport--availability-2) returns an [`OpenDlssNrSupport.Availability`](graphics.md#opendlssnrsupport-kt--opendlssnrsupport--availability) that is ready only when
the device enabled the required Vulkan features and the pinned weights and kernels are on disk; its
`reason` names the Gradle task to run when they are missing (`fetchOpenDlssNrWeights`,
`buildOpenDlssNrNative`). The paths can be overridden with `FIELD_OPEN_DLSS_NR_MODEL` and
`FIELD_OPEN_DLSS_NR_SHADERS`.

## CappedTwistFixture.kt { #cappedtwistfixture-kt }

A closed, rigged tube: the fixture for measuring what a twist costs a limb in volume.

[`RiggedFixture`](graphics.md#riggedfixture-kt-riggedfixture)'s bending cylinder is an open tube, so it encloses nothing and Manifold will not
accept it as a solid. This is the same two-bone rig with both ends capped and its rings four
times as close along the bone, so a 180° twist spreads over eight blended bands rather than one
and the volume that goes missing is the blend's doing rather than the triangulation's. At rest
the tube is a straight prism over a regular 12-gon, so its volume has a closed form and
`REST_VOLUME` is exactly 3.

Nothing is committed for this rig: `locate` writes the generated text to a temporary file named
after its hash, so a changed generator cannot be answered by a stale copy.
[A twisted limb, weighed and traced](../chain_skinned_volume.md) is this fixture posed, weighed
and path-traced.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/CappedTwistFixture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CappedTwistFixture/)

## CompressedSplatPly.kt { #compressedsplatply-kt }

Reads PlayCanvas's quantized `.compressed.ply` splat files back into ordinary per-splat floats.

Nothing upstream of this file has to know the format exists. `readPlyAsFloatTable` recognises the
schema from the file's own header and routes here, and what comes back carries the columns an
uncompressed 3D Gaussian splatting PLY would have given, in the same conventions. The unpacking
itself is [`CompressedSplatPly`](graphics.md#compressedsplatply-kt-compressedsplatply): the per-chunk ranges, the bit layouts, and the inverse of each
quantization. `readRaw` hands back the packed words instead, for a tool that wants to repack a
file rather than draw it.

## CompressedSplatPlyWriter.kt { #compressedsplatplywriter-kt }

How an edited splat cloud leaves Field, in the PlayCanvas `.compressed.ply` format it arrived in.

Box code reaches the object below through [`SplatCloud.write`](graphics.md#splatcloudedit-kt--splatcloud--write) for a file and
[`SplatCloud.toRawSplats`](graphics.md#splatcloudedit-kt--splatcloud--torawsplats) for the packed tables a renderer uploads. Both run the same encoder over
the same ordering, so what a preview shows and what a save contains are quantized alike.
[`CompressedSplatPly`](graphics.md#compressedsplatply-kt-compressedsplatply) is the reader this inverts.

Quantization is per chunk of 256 splats against that chunk's own bounds, which makes a splat's
accuracy a question of how tightly its neighbours in *file order* bound it. That is what
[`CompressedSplatPlyWriter.write`](graphics.md#compressedsplatplywriter-kt--compressedsplatplywriter--write)'s default Morton sort is for.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPlyWriter.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPlyWriter/)

## DualQuaternionSkinning.kt { #dualquaternionskinning-kt }

The second of Field's two skinning blends: joint motions averaged as dual quaternions, for rigs
that twist far enough to break the usual one.

Most callers arrive here without naming the file. [`GltfSkinning.skin`](graphics.md#gltfskinning-kt--gltfskinning--skin) is the entry point, and
passing it `SkinningOptions(method = SkinningMethod.DUAL_QUATERNION)` hands the vertices
straight to [`DualQuaternionSkinning.skin`](graphics.md#dualquaternionskinning-kt--dualquaternionskinning--skin), which takes the same arguments and returns the same
type. Linear blending averages the joint matrices, which is what every other engine defaults to
and what the GPU path does by default; it holds up until two influences disagree by a large
rotation, at which point the average of two rotations stops being a rotation and the
cross-section of a twisted limb flattens. Averaging rigid motions instead keeps it round.

Three things qualify that, and [`DualQuaternionSkinning`](graphics.md#dualquaternionskinning-kt-dualquaternionskinning) sets out each of them with its
measurement. A dual quaternion is a rigid motion and nothing else, so a joint that scales or
shears needs a residual matrix carried beside it. Two influences stored with opposite signs
cancel rather than average, unless one of them is chosen as a pivot and the others are flipped
to agree with it. And the comparison with linear blending is a trade rather than a win: this
bulges a joint ring where linear blending pinches it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/DualQuaternionSkinning.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/DualQuaternionSkinning/)

## GltfSkinning.kt { #gltfskinning-kt }

Skeletal animation on the CPU: bones, joint palettes and linear blend skinning, for a rigged file
loaded through Assimp.

[`GltfSkinning`](graphics.md#gltfskinning-kt-gltfskinning) reads the scene's node tree and its bones, samples one clip at a time, composes
each joint's palette entry down the parent chain, and blends the vertices. The short way in is
`skinnedGltfToTriMesh`: give it a file, a clip name and a time, and it returns the posed surface
as a `TriMesh` in scene space, ready to measure, trace or write back out. [`CpuSkinner`](graphics.md#skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt-cpuskinner) is the
same maths against a live mesh, deforming into the vertex buffer the renderer uploads.

[`GpuSkinning`](graphics.md#gpuskinning-kt-gpuskinning) carries the palette to the GPU and blends in the vertex shader, which is what a
crowd needs, and takes this file as its oracle. Where linear blending fails is a twist about a
bone's own axis, which pinches the joint ring to nothing: [`DualQuaternionSkinning`](graphics.md#dualquaternionskinning-kt-dualquaternionskinning) is the
alternative blend, and [A twisted limb, weighed and traced](../chain_skinned_volume.md) weighs
the difference between the two.

## GpuSkinning.kt { #gpuskinning-kt }

Skinning in the vertex shader: one mesh, one draw call, and a crowd of characters each posed
differently.

The bind-pose vertices are uploaded once and never touched again. Per frame the CPU writes only
the joint palette, which is instances times bones matrices, and the GPU does the per-vertex
blend, so a hundred characters cost a hundred palettes rather than a hundred deformations.
[`GpuSkinner`](graphics.md#gpuskinning-kt-gpuskinner) is the box-facing half: build one over a loaded `GltfSupport.MeshInstance`, hand it
a palette per instance with `uploadPalettes`, then `bindTo` the mesh you are drawing.
[`GpuSkinning`](graphics.md#gpuskinning-kt-gpuskinning) holds the GLSL and the palette packing underneath it.

The CPU path in [`GltfSkinning`](graphics.md#gltfskinning-kt-gltfskinning) is the oracle. The same GLSL that draws also runs as a compute
shader writing deformed positions to a buffer the CPU reads back, so a test that compares the two
is checking the shader that renders rather than a second implementation written to pass it.
Linear blending and dual quaternions can be mixed inside one draw call, chosen per instance,
which is the clearest way to see what separates them.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/GpuSkinning.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/GpuSkinning/)

## GpuSkinningEvidence.kt { #gpuskinningevidence-kt }

A program that draws GPU-skinned characters through the real Vulkan path and writes the frames
out as PNGs, each one paired with a CPU-skinned frame of the same pose.

```diffstatic {data-lang=bash}
./gradlew --no-daemon runGpuSkinningEvidence
```

It opens a window, poses a rigged fixture bent, blended across two clips, as a crowd of
instances and twisted, and writes the pictures under `dev_docs/agents/evidence/gpu_skinning`.
Each pose is rendered twice so that the two frames can be differenced: they differ in where the
skinning happened and in nothing else, which makes the difference a statement about the vertex
shader rather than about two renderers. A zero difference is weak on its own, so a control
frame with skinning switched off has to look different from the skinned one.

Every check ends the run with a non-zero exit code when it fails, including a frame that came
back blank, so this reads as a gate as well as a set of pictures. [`SkinningEvidence`](graphics.md#skinningevidence-kt-skinningevidence) is the
CPU-side companion, drawn with the software rasteriser.

## LoadPly.kt { #loadply-kt }

Reads one element of a PLY file as a flat table of floats, addressed by property name.

This is the column-oriented half of Field's PLY support, and the Gaussian splat path reads
through it: `gaussianSplats` and `SplatCloud.read` both arrive at `readPlyAsFloatTable`, then ask
for the columns they want by name. Every scalar property is widened to a float whatever it was on
disk, and list properties are read past and dropped, so a mesh's faces do not survive the trip.
For triangles, and a module to draw them with, load through `PlySupport.loadPly` instead.

A compressed PlayCanvas splat file is recognised from its header and decompressed on the way
through, so a caller sees the same columns either way; see [`CompressedSplatPly`](graphics.md#compressedsplatply-kt-compressedsplatply).

Nothing in the tree calls this yet; it is here for narrowing a wide table down to the few columns a GPU buffer wants. |

## MeshFromDisk.kt { #meshfromdisk-kt }

Connects the loaders that read geometry off disk to the CPU renderer that can *look* at it.

Field has four things that read geometry from a file, and one of them feeds the CPU preview:

 - `afield.geometry.mesh.mesh_io.kt` reads OBJ and STL straight into [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh) — the type
   [`afield.geometry.mesh.showMesh`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--showmesh), [`TriMesh.renderPng`](graphics.md#mesh-field-kt--renderpng) and the inline `toHTML()` card all render.
 - [`PlySupport`](graphics.md#simpleplysupport-kt-plysupport) reads PLY (ASCII, binary, both endians, colours, normals, point clouds) into a
   packed 10-float GPU buffer.
 - [`GltfSupport`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt-gltfsupport) reads glTF/GLB — and, being `Assimp.aiImportFile` underneath, also FBX, DAE, 3DS,
   OBJ, STL and PLY — into a packed 12-float GPU buffer plus materials.
 - `afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.FabricateGltfBridge` takes that same model into the PBR `StandardRenderer`.

Both GPU loaders produce plain host memory — `memAlloc`, not a Vulkan allocation — which is what
lets their output be read back into a [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh) on the CPU: [`PlySupport.PlyModel.toTriMesh`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--totrimesh),
[`assimpToTriMesh`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--assimptotrimesh) and the dispatcher [`meshFromAnyFile`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--meshfromanyfile), plus a [`Box.showMesh`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--showmesh) overload that takes
a `File`.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
showMesh(File("/path/to/thing.glb"))                     // straight to the orbitable viewer
val m = meshFromAnyFile("/path/to/scan.ply")             // or keep the mesh and compute with it
println(m.summary())
```

They live here rather than in `afield.stdlib` because `mesh_io.kt` carries no LWJGL dependency and
these need one. `afield.graphics.scene.*` is in every box's default imports
(see `afield.document.graph.intro`), so a box can call them without an import anyway.

What is *not* here, because nothing in the tree can read it: **STEP / IGES / BREP**. There is no CAD
kernel on the classpath, and those formats need NURBS-to-mesh tessellation rather than a parser —
see `public/docs/geometry_from_disk.md` for the full list of what does and does not load.

## PlyLoaderUnitTest.kt { #plyloaderunittest-kt }

Twelve checks over Field's PLY readers, as a standalone program that needs no Vulkan device.

It writes its own files into a temporary directory and reads them back: ASCII and binary meshes
in both byte orders, a point cloud, a file carrying neither colours nor normals, the float-table
view ([`PlyFloatTable`](graphics.md#loadply-kt-plyfloattable)), and the compressed Gaussian-splat format. One of those compressed files
has its packed words written out as literal bit patterns, so the reader is measured against the
format rather than against a second implementation of it; the others are round-tripped through
the writer.

Each check prints a line and the run ends in `All tests PASSED`, which is what the smoke catalog
matches on as `four.ply-loader.smoke`.

## RiggedFixture.kt { #riggedfixture-kt }

The rigged glTF files the skinning tests pose, generated by this source rather than downloaded.

The repository ships no rigged model, and skinning cannot be tested without one, so these two
write their own: glTF 2.0 text with the buffer inline as a base64 data URI, the same bytes on
every call. [`RiggedFixture`](graphics.md#riggedfixture-kt-riggedfixture) is the well-behaved case, a two-bone bending cylinder whose constants
are chosen so the bind pose comes out exact in binary, which lets a test assert bit-identity
against the unskinned mesh instead of a tolerance. [`StressFixture`](graphics.md#riggedfixture-kt-stressfixture) is the awkward one: a joint
that scales instead of rotating, so it shears a tilted plate; three vertices carrying six
influences where only four fit; and a skinned mesh node with a transform that glTF says to
ignore. Each of those arrives with the number it should produce.

Both commit their asset under `dev_docs/agents/fixtures/skinning/`, and `locate` returns an
absolute path to it from wherever the server happens to be running. [`CappedTwistFixture`](graphics.md#cappedtwistfixture-kt-cappedtwistfixture) is the
third rig, a closed tube for measuring volume.

## SkinnedMeshFromDisk.kt { #skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt }

Posing a rigged glTF on the CPU: into a fresh [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh), or back into the vertex buffer a loaded
model already owns.

Which of the two you want depends on what happens next. [`skinnedGltfToTriMesh`](graphics.md#skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt--skinnedgltftotrimesh) loads the file,
deforms it at one time and hands back geometry, which suits measuring a pose, feeding the
software rasteriser, or treating a frame as data. [`CpuSkinner`](graphics.md#skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt-cpuskinner) wraps a mesh that is already
loaded for drawing and overwrites its positions and normals in place, so the stock glTF shaders
draw a moving character without knowing that anything is being skinned.

[`posedGltfToTriMesh`](graphics.md#skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt--posedgltftotrimesh) is [`skinnedGltfToTriMesh`](graphics.md#skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt--skinnedgltftotrimesh) with the joint palette supplied by the caller,
for a clip blend or a pose an IK solver produced, and [`gltfClipNames`](graphics.md#skinnedmeshfromdisk-kt--gltfclipnames) reads the clip names out
of a file without deforming anything.

The blend itself is [`GltfSkinning`](graphics.md#gltfskinning-kt-gltfskinning)'s; what this file adds is the plumbing on either side of it.
[`GpuSkinner`](graphics.md#gpuskinning-kt-gpuskinner) moves the same work into the vertex shader, which is the path to take when the
character has to animate every frame.

## SkinningEvidence.kt { #skinningevidence-kt }

The evidence run behind Field's CPU glTF skinning: `./gradlew --no-daemon runSkinningEvidence`.

It writes the rigged fixture out as glTF, loads it back through the real Assimp path, and prints
what came back with the population each number was measured over: the skeleton and its clips, the
influence weights after the four-wide cap, whether the bind pose is bit-identical to the
unskinned mesh, and the displacement through the bend. A second, harder fixture covers the cases
that are easy to get wrong: a translated node that glTF says to ignore for a skinned mesh, a
shear whose correct vertex normal is known in closed form, and a vertex with six influences for
the cap to discard from. The run ends with a throughput figure in nanoseconds per vertex, with
and without exact inverse-transpose normals.

Frames go to `dev_docs/agents/evidence/skinning/` for a person to look at, named by
[`SkinningEvidence.frames`](graphics.md#skinningevidence-kt--skinningevidence--frames) so the sequence reads in sorted order, and the numbers are the ones
`dev_docs/SKINNED_CHARACTERS.md` quotes. [`GpuSkinningEvidence`](graphics.md#gpuskinningevidence-kt-gpuskinningevidence) is the same exercise for the
compute-shader path.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/SkinningEvidence.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/SkinningEvidence/)

## simpleGLTFSupport.kt { #simplegltfsupport-kt }

Loading a model file onto the GPU, with its materials and textures.

`gltfModelHere("model.glb") { }` in a box is the usual case: the call
expands the way `moduleHere` does, into a graphics module carrying the bundled glTF shaders at the
end of this file, and hands back that module together with the loaded [`GltfSupport.GltfModel`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt--gltfsupport--gltfmodel).
[`GltfSupport.loadGltfBasic`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt--gltfsupport--loadgltfbasic) is the same load without a module, for code bringing its own shaders.

The name says glTF and the importer is Assimp, so the formats are Assimp's: glTF and GLB, and also
FBX, DAE, OBJ, STL and PLY. A load returns one [`GltfSupport.MeshInstance`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt--gltfsupport--meshinstance) per mesh in the node tree,
each carrying host-side vertex and index buffers in the fixed 12-float layout those shaders read
(position, normal, uv, colour), its material, and the node's animation track resampled at a fixed
rate, which this file's `sample` extension interpolates at whatever time you ask for.

Two things catch callers out. [`GltfSupport.GltfLoadConfig`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt--gltfsupport--gltfloadconfig)'s `loadTextures` is on by default and
that path asks the box context for a [`Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer), so a load taking the default arguments cannot run
outside a live renderer; pass `GltfLoadConfig(loadTextures = false)` for geometry alone, as
[`assimpToTriMesh`](graphics.md#meshfromdisk-kt--assimptotrimesh) does. And a [`GltfSupport.MeshInstance`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt--gltfsupport--meshinstance)'s `bindPose` is a
translation/rotation/scale triple, which cannot hold the mirror or shear a glTF node transform is
allowed to carry; `bindMatrix`, documented at length below, is the full 4×4 the loader also keeps.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/simpleGLTFSupport.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/simpleGLTFSupport/)

## simplePLYSupport.kt { #simpleplysupport-kt }

Loads a PLY mesh or point cloud into a live Vulkan module, shaders included.

In a box, `plyModelHere("model.ply")` is the whole of it: the macro builds a module wired to the
bundled shaders, loads the file, and returns both the module and the loaded model. Point clouds
take `plyPointCloudHere`, which draws every point as a screen-aligned quad that the fragment
shader rounds off into a dot. Underneath, [`PlySupport`](graphics.md#simpleplysupport-kt-plysupport) is a plain reader, ASCII or binary PLY in
either endianness, and it will load a file with no renderer in sight.

For a `TriMesh` to compute with rather than a module to draw, `meshFromAnyFile` reads the same
files; see [Geometry from disk](../geometry_from_disk.md). Gaussian splats are the other
direction: their PLY carries a rotation and a scale per splat rather than faces, and
`readPlyAsFloatTable` is what reads it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/simplePLYSupport.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/simplePLYSupport/)

**Used in:** [Geometry from disk](../geometry_from_disk.md)

## Introspection.kt { #introspection-kt }

Reflection of a compiled shader's interface: the uniform blocks, storage buffers, textures, images,
acceleration structures and push constants it declares, with their sets, bindings, member offsets and
sizes.

[`Introspection`](graphics.md#introspection-kt-introspection) compiles GLSL to SPIR-V through [`ShaderSPIRVUtils`](graphics.md#shaderspirvutils-kt-shaderspirvutils) (or takes SPIR-V or Slang reflection
directly, through `fromSpirv` and `fromSlangReflection`) and reads the result with SPIRV-Cross, so the
layout it reports is the compiler's, not a parse of the source. [`Introspected`](graphics.md#introspection-kt-introspected) holds the reflected
types; [`parseGlslMemberComments`](graphics.md#introspection-kt--parseglslmembercomments) recovers the trailing comments on block members, which the
reflection does not carry. Field's modules use this to allocate and bind each shader's buffers.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/Introspection.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/Introspection/)

## ShaderAbi.kt { #shaderabi-kt }

Decides whether a recompiled shader can be swapped in without a full reload.

[`graphicsShaderAbiCheck`](graphics.md#shaderabi-kt--graphicsshaderabicheck) and [`computeShaderAbiCheck`](graphics.md#shaderabi-kt--computeshaderabicheck) compare the old and new [`Introspection`](graphics.md#introspection-kt-introspection) of each
stage; a changed interface in any stage returns a [`ShaderAbiCheck`](graphics.md#shaderabi-kt-shaderabicheck) that is not compatible, with a
message asking for a full reload.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/ShaderAbi.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/ShaderAbi/)

## ShaderInterfaceTransition.kt { #shaderinterfacetransition-kt }

What changed in a shader's interface across a full reload, binding by binding and member by member.

[`shaderInterfaceTransition`](graphics.md#shaderinterfacetransition-kt--shaderinterfacetransition) and [`graphicsShaderInterfaceTransition`](graphics.md#shaderinterfacetransition-kt--graphicsshaderinterfacetransition) compare two [`Introspection`](graphics.md#introspection-kt-introspection)s and
classify each binding as one [`ShaderBindingChange`](graphics.md#shaderinterfacetransition-kt-shaderbindingchange); the result names what was kept, added, removed,
renamed, resized or retyped, so a reload can re-apply the values that still fit. Tested in
`ShaderInterfaceTransitionTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/ShaderInterfaceTransition.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/ShaderInterfaceTransition/)

## ShaderSPIRVUtils.kt { #shaderspirvutils-kt }

GLSL to SPIR-V compilation through shaderc, with `#include` resolution and line-numbered error reports.

[`ShaderSPIRVUtils`](graphics.md#shaderspirvutils-kt-shaderspirvutils) compiles a source for one [`ShaderKind`](graphics.md#shaderspirvutils-kt-shaderkind) (vertex, fragment, compute, mesh, task and
the ray-tracing stages), and throws [`CompilerError`](graphics.md#shaderspirvutils-kt-compilererror) with the compiler's message on failure. A
[`ShaderIncludeResolver`](graphics.md#shaderspirvutils-kt-shaderincluderesolver) passed in a [`ShaderCompileSource`](graphics.md#shaderspirvutils-kt-shadercompilesource) answers each include request.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/ShaderSPIRVUtils.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/ShaderSPIRVUtils/)

## ShadertoyChannels.kt { #shadertoychannels-kt }

What a ShaderToy Image pass reads and draws onto in Field: [`ShadertoyChannel`](graphics.md#shadertoychannels-kt-shadertoychannel) (a texture turned the
way ShaderToy samples one), [`ShadertoyCanvas`](graphics.md#shadertoychannels-kt-shadertoycanvas) (the picture a document's shadertoy boxes share, shown
in the renderer window) and [`webcam`](graphics.md#shadertoychannels-kt--webcam) (the camera as a channel).

`shadertoyHere` builds the module; these give it inputs and somewhere to draw. The `shadertrinket`
starting point uses all three:

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val canvas = shadertoyCanvas()
canvas += shadertoyHere {
    +canvas.rtt
    textures("iChannel0" to webcam())
}
```

## SlangCompiler.kt { #slangcompiler-kt }

Compiles Slang shaders by running an external `slangc`, to GLSL, SPIR-V and reflection JSON.

[`SlangCompiler`](graphics.md#slangcompiler-kt-slangcompiler) looks for the executable in `AFIELD_SLANGC`, then `-Dafield.slangc`, then the pinned
download, the Vulkan SDK and `PATH`. `compileVertexFragment` and `compileSharedStage` return one
[`SlangStageArtifacts`](graphics.md#slangcompiler-kt-slangstageartifacts) per stage, ready for [`Introspection`](graphics.md#introspection-kt-introspection).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/SlangCompiler.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/SlangCompiler/)

## GpuShaderLearningView.kt { #gpushaderlearningview-kt }

An editable render-to-texture teacher next to a learner that trains on the GPU while it runs.

[`GpuShaderLearningView`](graphics.md#gpushaderlearningview-kt-gpushaderlearningview) pairs a source [`RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture) with [`GpuShaderTraining`](graphics.md#gpushadertraining-kt-gpushadertraining); with [`learning`](graphics.md#gpushaderlearningview-kt--gpushaderlearningview--learning) off and the
learned-only view selected, the source stops running and the learned function stays.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderLearningView.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderLearningView/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GpuShaderLearningView</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RenderToTexture</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;gpu-learning&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">setSourceParameter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Target</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderLearningView/#L27)

## GpuShaderTraining.kt { #gpushadertraining-kt }

On-GPU training of the learned RGB function, with no CPU image or weight readback.

[`GpuShaderTraining`](graphics.md#gpushadertraining-kt-gpushadertraining) is the in-renderer alternative to the offline [`ShaderTraining`](graphics.md#shadertraining-kt-shadertraining) path. It needs a device with cooperative-vector training enabled and the prebuilt training shaders under `build/lighting/learned-shader/`; otherwise its constructor refuses and the offline path remains.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderTraining.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderTraining/)

### GpuShaderTraining { #gpushadertraining-kt-gpushadertraining }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GpuShaderTraining</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">batchSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">256</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderTraining/#L42)

A small reusable learned RGB function, trained directly from Field images on the graphics queue. Architecture matches LearnedShader: 16 positional features -> 32 ReLU -> 32 ReLU -> RGB. Slang differentiates the network; cooperative-vector outer products accumulate its gradients. FP32 Adam master weights/moments, loss-scaled FP16 gradients and inference matrices. The source remains caller-owned. Train/evaluate/close only between or within render-thread work. No CPU image/weight readback is used in train/evaluate. This is not a general graph ML runtime.

## LearnedShader.kt { #learnedshader-kt }

Runs a trained shader function as a compute pass that writes its own render target.

[`LearnedShader`](graphics.md#learnedshader-kt-learnedshader) loads a model directory written by training, evaluates it each frame for the current parameter, and
can [`LearnedShader.attach`](graphics.md#learnedshader-kt--learnedshader--attach) itself to the renderer's pre-target list. It uses cooperative vectors when the device
supports them and a scalar variant otherwise.

## ShaderLearningChecks.kt { #shaderlearningchecks-kt }

Acceptance checks for a learned shader, run from a box beneath the moduleHere starting point once training finishes.

[`ShaderLearningChecks.run`](graphics.md#shaderlearningchecks-kt--shaderlearningchecks--run) measures a [`ShaderLearningView`](graphics.md#shaderlearningview-kt-shaderlearningview) at a held-out parameter: full-image error, timing, and whether a rejected model leaves the previous one attached. [`ShaderLearningChecks.stripeMetrics`](graphics.md#shaderlearningchecks-kt--shaderlearningchecks--stripemetrics) measures error at the bundled test pattern's hard stripe edge separately, because a whole-image mean can hide edge smoothing.

## ShaderTraining.kt { #shadertraining-kt }

Offline distillation of a Field render target into a small learned shader: capture samples, then train them in Python.

[`ShaderTraining.capture`](graphics.md#shadertraining-kt--shadertraining--capture) renders the source [`RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture) across a parameter range and writes train and held-out sample files, keyed by a digest of the source's shaders. [`ShaderTraining.trainAsync`](graphics.md#shadertraining-kt--shadertraining--trainasync) runs `tools/lighting/train_shader.py` through `uv` as a child process and returns a [`ShaderTrainingJob`](graphics.md#shadertraining-kt-shadertrainingjob) whose `result` completes with the model directory. The source shaders keep running in Vulkan; only their output images reach Python.

## shaders.kt { #shaders-kt }

The bridge between a box's text and a live Vulkan pipeline: shader source lives in box
properties, and this file turns it into modules and keeps them hot-reloading.

The properties come first — `vertex`, `fragment`, `compute`, `task`/`mesh`, the ray-tracing
stages, and a `_s` variant of each for Slang — alongside `once.vertex { }`-style seeders. The
user-facing entry points are the macro placeholders [`Box.moduleHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--modulehere), [`Box.computeModuleHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--computemodulehere),
[`Box.meshModuleHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--meshmodulehere), [`Box.rayTracingModuleHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--raytracingmodulehere) and [`Box.shadertoyHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--shadertoyhere); each one throws
`MacroNotExpandedException` if actually called, because `MacroRegistry` is expected to rewrite it
into the real `_moduleHere`-family call.

Before compilation every stage goes through [`preprocess`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--preprocess), which resolves `{% property %}` template
tags against other boxes' shader properties (with cycle detection and `#line` fixups) and against
built-in includes such as the field probe, field stats and quantile warp. Registered include roots —
[`registerShaderFilesystemIncludeRoot`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--registershaderfilesystemincluderoot) for a directory, [`registerLygiaIncludeRoot`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--registerlygiaincluderoot) /
[`shaderCachedUrlIncludeRootResolver`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--shadercachedurlincluderootresolver) for URL-fetched, disk-cached libraries — are **not** reachable
from here: they are resolved by shaderc during compilation, from a real `#include` only. It also expands
`{% copyPC %}` (copying a previous stage's push-constant block) and stackAuto template slots
compiled from StackSL via [`stackAutoShaderSource`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--stackautoshadersource).

[`reloadShader`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--reloadshader), [`reloadComputeShader`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--reloadcomputeshader), [`reloadMeshShader`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--reloadmeshshader) and [`reloadRayTracingShader`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--reloadraytracingshader) are the
reload path: compile, report errors back onto the box's source lines, introspect the result, and
rewrite the box's Kotlin preamble with generated binding structures before swapping the module.
[`Box.attachShader`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--attachshader) adopts an externally built module into that same path. [`Box.fieldProbeHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--fieldprobehere),
[`Box.fieldStatsHere`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--fieldstatshere) and [`Box.fieldProbeAutoControl`](graphics.md#shaders-kt--fieldprobeautocontrol) attach the GPU readback instrumentation.

Everything here needs a live `Box` — properties, error reporting, preamble edits and the
generation-guarded async reload all key off it.

## SlugBuffer.kt { #slugbuffer-kt }

The GPU side of Slug filled-path rendering: [`SlugBuffer`](graphics.md#slugbuffer-kt-slugbuffer) holds one [`SlugPath`](graphics.md#slugpath-kt-slugpath)'s atlas words in a
Vulkan storage buffer that a slug shader reads.

[`SlugBuffer.replace`](graphics.md#slugbuffer-kt--slugbuffer--replace) swaps in new geometry behind the same buffer supplier, so existing shader
bindings keep working, and [`SlugBuffer.close`](graphics.md#slugbuffer-kt--slugbuffer--close) falls back to a shared empty atlas that draws
nothing. `SlugRenderSmoke` exercises it against a live renderer.

## SlugPath.kt { #slugpath-kt }

Compiles a filled, flat [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline) into Slughorn atlas data ([`SlugPath`](graphics.md#slugpath-kt-slugpath)) by running the native
`field-slug` helper, built with `./gradlew buildSlugNative`.

`SlugPath.compile` runs once per geometry edit, not per frame, and refuses paths that leave
z=0. The result is immutable and carries no placement; [`SlugBuffer`](graphics.md#slugbuffer-kt-slugbuffer) uploads it to the GPU.
`SlugPathTest` covers it.

## typography.kt { #typography-kt }

Text as geometry: a string becomes contours, and from there everything Field already does to
geometry applies to letters.

A layout here is a value you can extrude, march, sample or animate, not a label painted into a
raster — which is what every other use of `java.awt.Font` in the tree does (`MeshGallery`,
`ImagingGallery`, `montage`'s 5x7 bitmap font). It needs no dependency beyond AWT:
`Font.createGlyphVector(...).getOutline()` hands back real quadratic/cubic glyph outlines, and it
works headless. `typography_field.kt` is the bridge to Field's own 2D and 3D outputs.

### The three values

 - [`Typeface`](graphics.md#typography-kt-typeface) — a font at a size, from a logical/system name ([`typeface`](graphics.md#typography-kt--typeface)) or a `.ttf`/`.otf` on
   disk ([`typefaceFromFile`](graphics.md#typography-kt--typefacefromfile)). Carries the vertical metrics (ascent, descent, leading) a layout
   needs.
 - [`Glyph`](graphics.md#typography-kt-glyph) — one glyph's outline, cached per typeface and glyph code, in its own frame with its
   origin on its own baseline. Both representations live side by side: [`Glyph.contours`](graphics.md#typography-kt--glyph--contours) are
   flattened, nesting-classified, winding-normalised polygons for geometry work, and
   [`Glyph.outline`](graphics.md#typography-kt--glyph--outline) is the same rings as an [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline) of *real cubics* for drawing.
 - [`TextLayout`](graphics.md#typography-kt-textlayout) — glyphs placed on baselines by AWT's own advances and kerning, plus tracking,
   multi-line and alignment. Every glyph in it is a [`PlacedGlyph`](graphics.md#typography-kt-placedglyph) carrying **mutable transform
   handles** (offset, rotation, scale, pivot). Those handles are how you animate letters
   individually, and [`TextLayout.onCurve`](graphics.md#typography-kt--oncurve) is nothing but a routine that sets them from an
   [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline)'s arc length.

### Text space

Glyph and layout coordinates are **x right, y down**, origin at the first baseline, units = the
typeface's size in points. That is AWT's own glyph frame and it is also the frame Field's 2D
outputs use (`Rect`'s y grows downwards), so text handed straight to `Box.lines` or
[`Box.showText`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--showtext) reads the right way up with no transform. The 3D bridges in `typography_field.kt`
flip y at their own boundary, because a mesh wants y up.

### The winding convention

A glyph's counter — the hole in `o`, `e`, `a`, `B` — is only a hole if something says so, and what
the font shipped is not enough to go on. (`isoContourFLines` in `contours.kt` leaves winding
arbitrary, and every consumer downstream has to cope.) So this file *decides*:

> For a ring `p0..pn`, signed area is `½Σ(xᵢyᵢ₊₁ − xᵢ₊₁yᵢ)` in text space. **Outer contours are
> positive; holes are negative.** A ring's [`GlyphContour.depth`](graphics.md#typography-kt--glyphcontour--depth) — how many other rings of the same
> glyph contain it — is authoritative: even depth is an outer contour, odd depth is a hole. A ring
> whose area sign disagrees with its depth is *reversed* on the way out.

Both representations obey it, so `contours.filter { it.isHole }` and the subpaths of
[`Glyph.outline`](graphics.md#typography-kt--glyph--outline) agree, and `TypographyTest` asserts it on glyphs whose answer is known by eye
(`o` has one hole, `l` has none, `%` has two).

### AWT and the main run loop

`imaging_field.kt` captions `montage` with a bitmap table instead of `Graphics2D.drawString`, for
a reason that reaches this file: on macOS, touching the AWT font manager pulls in AppKit, which
competes with GLFW for the main run loop, and `Server.main` never initialises the toolkit. This
family cannot avoid the font manager — it *is* the font manager — so it contains the hazard in one
place, [`Typefaces.warm`](graphics.md#typography-kt--typefaces--warm), whose KDoc carries the measured stack trace and the conclusion:

> **A JVM that wants glyph outlines and passes `-XstartOnFirstThread` must also pass
> `-Djava.awt.headless=true`.** Otherwise `CFontManager.loadFonts` dispatches to the process's first
> thread and waits forever for a run loop nobody is pumping.

[`Typefaces.warm`](graphics.md#typography-kt--typefaces--warm) detects that in four seconds and throws with that sentence in it, rather than
hanging the editor. Every jvm-main gallery in the tree already sets the property in the first line
of `main`, `jvmTest` does not need it (Gradle's test JVM has no `-XstartOnFirstThread`), and an
interactive Field window pumps its run loop through `glfwPollEvents` and so is expected to be
fine — expected, not tested; see [`Typefaces.warm`](graphics.md#typography-kt--typefaces--warm). Everything after that one touch is pure
computation over cached outlines.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/text/typography.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/text/typography/)

## typography_field.kt { #typography-field-kt }

The bridges out of a [`TextLayout`](graphics.md#typography-kt-textlayout) and into the four families Field already has.

`typography.kt` answers with *structure* — rings, depths, advances, handles — and structure is not
yet a drawing, a mesh, an image or a point cloud. This file converts it: once a string is
contours, letters are inputs to machinery that never knew about text.

It is the typographic counterpart of `spatial_field.kt` (plane geometry → `FLine`) and
`mesh_field.kt` (`TriMesh` → `FLine`), and it is written to the same rule: every function here
returns a *value* — no `Box`, no output — except the two figure helpers at the bottom, which are
`drawToSVG` and so work headless, in a test and in the docs build.

Five bridges:

 1. **→ [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline)** ([`TextLayout.toFLines`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--toflines), [`TextLayout.toFLine`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--tofline), [`Glyph.toFLine`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--tofline)). One line per
    glyph, so a per-glyph handle actually moves something, with the font's real cubics intact.
    Filling works because of `typography.kt`'s winding convention and nothing else: Skia and
    Java2D both fill non-zero, so a counter is a hole precisely because its ring runs the other
    way. [`TextLayout.toFLines`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--toflines) takes `honourHoles = false` to show you the blob you get without a
    convention, which is the control arm the docs figure uses.
 2. **→ [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh)** ([`TextLayout.toMesh`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--tomesh)). Hole-aware extrusion: [`extrudeMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-generate-kt--extrudemesh) and
    [`triangulatePolygon`](graphics.md#mesh-generate-kt--triangulatepolygon) each take a single ring and cannot do holes, so the
    caps here go through `FloatEarcut` with hole indices and the walls are emitted ring by ring
    from the *same* flattened vertices, which is what makes the result watertight — and makes an
    extruded `o` genus 1 and an extruded `l` genus 0.
 3. **→ an SDF** ([`TextLayout.toSdf`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--tosdf)). A 2D signed-distance grid, bilinearly sampled and extruded
    in z, so letters compose with `sdfSphere`, `sdfSmoothUnion`, `.twisted()` and everything else
    in `mesh_sdf.kt`, and `marchingCubes` will mesh the result.
 4. **→ [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img)** ([`rasterizeText`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--rasterizetext)). An analytic even-odd scanline fill of the layout's own rings —
    *not* `Graphics2D.drawString`, both because a stdlib call every box might make must not be
    able to initialise AWT's font manager and because filling our own outlines means a legible PNG
    is evidence about *this* code rather than about AWT's rasteriser.
 5. **→ points** ([`TextLayout.samplePoints`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--samplepoints), [`TextLayout.toPointFLine`](graphics.md#typography-field-kt--topointfline)). Even-by-arc-length
    samples along the outlines, which is what the alife agents, the clusterers and the
    contourers in `clustering.kt` / `alife_agents.kt` consume.

Frames: bridges 1, 3, 4 and 5 stay in text space (y **down**, origin on the first baseline);
bridge 2 flips y at its boundary, because a mesh wants y up, and re-normalises winding when it
does.

## Image.kt { #image-kt }

[`Image`](graphics.md#image-kt-image) wraps a `VkImage` and its memory, created from an [`Image.ImageData`](graphics.md#image-kt--image--imagedata) description, including the external-memory exports used to hand frames to other processes.

Alongside ordinary device-local images, an [`Image`](graphics.md#image-kt-image) can be allocated for export as an opaque fd
(CUDA/NVENC on Linux, see [`VulkanExternalMemory`](graphics.md#vulkanexternalmemory-kt-vulkanexternalmemory)), as a dma-buf with a DRM format modifier (see
[`LinuxDmaBufExport`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt-linuxdmabufexport)) or as a Metal IOSurface (see [`MetalIOSurface`](graphics.md#metaliosurfaceexport-kt-metaliosurface)). The file also holds the
format helpers [`vkFormatBytesPerPixel`](graphics.md#image-kt--vkformatbytesperpixel) and [`vkFormatBytesPerPixelOrNull`](graphics.md#image-kt--vkformatbytesperpixelornull), and
[`image_layout_transition`](graphics.md#image-kt--image-layout-transition) for recording layout barriers.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/Image.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/Image/)

| <a id="image-kt--image--exportopaquefd"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">exportOpaqueFd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/Image/#L345) | Export this image's backing memory as an opaque POSIX fd (Linux, VK_KHR_external_memory_fd, see [`VulkanExternalMemory`](graphics.md#vulkanexternalmemory-kt-vulkanexternalmemory)). Requires `exportOpaqueFd` set on the [`Image.ImageData`](graphics.md#image-kt--image--imagedata) it was created from. Per the spec each call to vkGetMemoryFdKHR transfers ownership of a *new* fd to the caller, so this caches and returns the same fd on repeated calls — call [`close`](imaging.md#imaging-features-kt--close) to release it, don't just drop the value. The fd stays valid (and open in this JVM process) for the streamer's whole session; the helper process only ever gets a *duplicate* via `/proc/<pid>/fd/<fd>` (see WIRE_FORMAT.md's Linux addendum), never this one. |

Requires `exportDmaBuf` set on the [`Image.ImageData`](graphics.md#image-kt--image--imagedata) it was created from. |

## ImageView.kt { #imageview-kt }

[`ImageView`](graphics.md#imageview-kt-imageview) wraps a `VkImageView` over an image, and the small interfaces Field's shader bindings use to find views and samplers.

[`HasImageView`](graphics.md#imageview-kt-hasimageview) and [`HasImageViewArray`](graphics.md#imageview-kt-hasimageviewarray) are what a texture binding accepts; [`PreparesSampledImages`](graphics.md#imageview-kt-preparessampledimages)
lets a source record its layout transitions before sampling, and [`HasDefaultTextureSampler`](graphics.md#imageview-kt-hasdefaulttexturesampler) carries
the sampler a binding uses when none is given.

## LinuxDmaBufExport.kt { #linuxdmabufexport-kt }

[`LinuxDmaBufExport`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt-linuxdmabufexport) exports Vulkan images as Linux dma-bufs described by a DRM format modifier, so another process (such as Electron) can import them without a copy.

[`LinuxDmaBufExport.shareableModifiers`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt--linuxdmabufexport--shareablemodifiers) and [`LinuxDmaBufExport.supportsModifier`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt--linuxdmabufexport--supportsmodifier) check which
modifiers the device can export for a format; [`LinuxDmaBufExport.handle`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt--linuxdmabufexport--handle) and
[`LinuxDmaBufExport.handles`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt--linuxdmabufexport--handles) package an exported image as a [`DmaBufHandle`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt-dmabufhandle) of fd, modifier and
[`DmaBufPlaneLayout`](graphics.md#linuxdmabufexport-kt-dmabufplanelayout)s. Linux only.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/LinuxDmaBufExport.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/LinuxDmaBufExport/)

### DmaBufPlaneLayout { #linuxdmabufexport-kt-dmabufplanelayout }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DmaBufPlaneLayout</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">offset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rowPitch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/LinuxDmaBufExport/#L39)

One DRM-modifier memory plane of a dma-buf image, as the importer must be told it: a byte offset into the allocation and a row pitch. These are *memory* planes of the modifier's layout, not colour planes of the format.

### DmaBufHandle { #linuxdmabufexport-kt-dmabufhandle }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DmaBufHandle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">fd</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">modifier</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">planes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">DmaBufPlaneLayout</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">size</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/LinuxDmaBufExport/#L50)

An exported dma-buf image: one POSIX fd owning the allocation, the DRM format modifier that describes its tiling, and every memory plane's layout. This is the same information an Electron `nativePixmap` carries, and it maps directly onto `afield.media.browser.ExternalBrowserImageHandle.LinuxDmaBuf`.

## MetalIOSurfaceExport.kt { #metaliosurfaceexport-kt }

[`MetalIOSurface`](graphics.md#metaliosurfaceexport-kt-metaliosurface) reaches the macOS IOSurface framework from Kotlin, so a Field render-to-texture image can be shared with another process by `IOSurfaceID` or Mach port.

It looks up, locks, measures and releases IOSurfaces, and [`MetalIOSurface.ioSurfaceIds`](graphics.md#metaliosurfaceexport-kt--metaliosurface--iosurfaceids) lists the
ids behind a [`afield.graphics.vulkan.targets.RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture) created for IOSurface export. macOS only.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/MetalIOSurfaceExport.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/MetalIOSurfaceExport/)

## UnixFdPass.kt { #unixfdpass-kt }

[`UnixFdPass`](graphics.md#unixfdpass-kt-unixfdpass) sends file descriptors to another process over a Unix domain socket with SCM_RIGHTS, which is how Field hands exported GPU memory to its Linux encoder helper.

It calls a separately built JNI helper (`native/field-fdpass/`), loaded through its own class
loader; [`UnixFdPass.available`](graphics.md#unixfdpass-kt--unixfdpass--available) reports whether that helper is present. Linux only.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass/)

Returns false on any failure (socket missing/not listening yet, connect refused, send failed) — callers should retry with backoff for the "not listening yet" race rather than fail immediately. |

## VulkanExternalMemory.kt { #vulkanexternalmemory-kt }

Exports a render-to-texture color image as a POSIX file descriptor, so the Linux
`field-encode-linux` helper can import it into CUDA and encode it with NVENC.

The chain: render into an RTT created with `exportOpaqueFd = true`, then [`Image.exportOpaqueFd`](graphics.md#image-kt--image--exportopaquefd)
(VK_KHR_external_memory_fd) yields an fd open in this JVM process, and
[`VulkanExternalMemory.handle`](graphics.md#vulkanexternalmemory-kt--vulkanexternalmemory--handle) packages it with the exact allocation size (CUDA's
cuImportExternalMemory requires an exact match) and the row pitch (NVENC's
NV_ENC_REGISTER_RESOURCE.pitch, which is the image's actual, possibly alignment-padded, linear
layout rather than width times bytes per pixel).

The fd number never travels over the JSON control channel, because a raw fd means nothing to
another process by value; a Mac IOSurfaceID, by contrast, is a system-wide handle.
`VulkanExternalMemory.FdHandle.fd` feeds [`UnixFdPass.sendFds`](graphics.md#unixfdpass-kt--unixfdpass--sendfds), which passes the kernel object to
the helper over SCM_RIGHTS, and only `size` and `rowPitch` go into the JSON of
`FieldEncodeProcess.open(fdSurfaces = ...)`.

`vkGetMemoryFdKHR` is an ordinary LWJGL Vulkan binding, so the export itself lives on [`Image`](graphics.md#image-kt-image);
this object is the `RenderToTexture`-level convenience, the counterpart of
[`MetalIOSurface.ioSurfaceIds`](graphics.md#metaliosurfaceexport-kt--metaliosurface--iosurfaceids) on macOS.

Linux/NVIDIA only. The fd stays open in this process for the streamer's session, and the helper
receives a duplicate of the kernel object, so this process must not close its own fd while
streaming. Design notes: `dev_docs/vision_frontend.md`, "The sender seam", Linux row.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/VulkanExternalMemory.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/VulkanExternalMemory/)

## MegaTexture.kt { #megatexture-kt }

A virtual texture over thousands of source images, paged into a fixed GPU atlas on demand.

Shaders report which images and detail levels they need through a feedback buffer; [`MegaTexture`](graphics.md#megatexture-kt-megatexture)
reads it back, asks [`MegaTextureDecoder`](graphics.md#megatexturedecoder-kt-megatexturedecoder) for the missing pages, copies them into atlas slots and
publishes a page table the shader samples through. [`MegaTextureConfig`](graphics.md#megatexture-kt-megatextureconfig) sets page size, residency
budget and feedback rate, and [`MegaTextureStats`](graphics.md#megatexture-kt-megatexturestats) reports per-level residency and decode queues.

## MegaTextureCatalog.kt { #megatexturecatalog-kt }

The stable image-to-index catalog behind a [`MegaTexture`](graphics.md#megatexture-kt-megatexture), and the on-disk pyramid cache keyed to it.

[`MegaTextureCatalog`](graphics.md#megatexturecatalog-kt-megatexturecatalog) assigns each source file an append-only index and detects files that changed
since the last run; [`MegaTexturePyramidCache`](graphics.md#megatexturecatalog-kt-megatexturepyramidcache) stores decoded pages so a later run can skip
decoding them.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/mega/MegaTextureCatalog.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/mega/MegaTextureCatalog/)

## MegaTextureDecoder.kt { #megatexturedecoder-kt }

Background decoding of source images into downsampled [`MegaTexture`](graphics.md#megatexture-kt-megatexture) pages.

[`MegaTextureDecoder`](graphics.md#megatexturedecoder-kt-megatexturedecoder) runs a prioritised worker pool that turns requests into [`MegaDecodedPage`](graphics.md#megatexturedecoder-kt-megadecodedpage)s,
drawing their pixel memory from per-level pools that the consumer returns with
[`MegaTextureDecoder.recycle`](graphics.md#megatexturedecoder-kt--megatexturedecoder--recycle).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/mega/MegaTextureDecoder.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/mega/MegaTextureDecoder/)

## MegaTextureLayout.kt { #megatexturelayout-kt }

The atlas geometry and page-table encoding for a [`MegaTexture`](graphics.md#megatexture-kt-megatexture), kept free of any GPU calls.

[`MegaTextureLayout`](graphics.md#megatexturelayout-kt-megatexturelayout) computes per-level page sizes and slot placement and packs page-table entries;
`MegaTextureLayoutTest` checks that arithmetic without a Vulkan device.
