### HtcEyeTrackingState { #openxreyetracking-kt-htceyetrackingstate }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">HtcEyeTrackingState</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OpenXREyeTracking/#L147)

HTC per-eye gaze, pupil and geometry observations, updated in place on the renderer's queue thread. The three streams have independent validity and OpenXR timestamps (nanoseconds). A failed stream does not suppress the other streams. Numeric values retain the last valid observation; timestamps reset to zero when a query fails or a frame is skipped.

Each of its three streams carries its own validity flag. |

## OpenXRHmdTarget.kt { #openxrhmdtarget-kt }

The OpenXR headset as a render target: [`OpenXRHmdTarget`](graphics.md#openxrhmdtarget-kt-openxrhmdtarget) acquires each eye's swapchain image,
renders registered modules into it, and submits the frame with a projection layer.

It uses the OpenXR session that the Vulkan instance creates when VR is enabled, and also reports
head and controller poses. Instead of rendering per eye, it can copy a side-by-side texture (from
[`SideBySideStereoTarget`](graphics.md#sidebysidestereotarget-kt-sidebysidestereotarget) or a wide [`RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture)) into the two eyes.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OpenXRHmdTarget.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OpenXRHmdTarget/)

### OpenXRHmdTarget { #openxrhmdtarget-kt-openxrhmdtarget }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OpenXRHmdTarget</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">fromContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OpenXRHmdTarget/#L160)

Found in the box graph by default. ## OwnedModules.kt { #ownedmodules-kt }

Ownership for the modules a box puts into a renderer's target maps, which is what
`renderer += "name" to module` records so that something can take the module out again.

The map belongs to the renderer and the module to the box that compiled it, a split the map alone
cannot express: a deleted box's module would otherwise go on drawing, holding the snippet
classloader that built it. Each put therefore files a lifecycle claim under
`afield.runtime.lifecycle.ReleasePolicy.KEYED`, so stopping the box leaves the module drawing, a
re-run under the same name replaces it, and retiring the box (delete, document close) removes it.
The claim is filed under the renderer as well, and disposing the renderer ends the ones whose
device has gone.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OwnedModules.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OwnedModules/)

## PingPongRenderToTexture.kt { #pingpongrendertotexture-kt }

Feedback rendering: [`PingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt-pingpongrendertotexture) keeps a ring of images per color attachment, so a
module can sample the previous frame while drawing the next.

Each frame renders into one slot of the ring and exposes the earlier, completed slots as
textures, which is the shape of trails, reaction-diffusion and other effects that read their own
last output. [`FrameCadencedPingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt-framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture) advances the ring only every few frames, for
a slow sequence that downstream code crossfades between.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">open</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PingPongRenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">fromContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RTTParameters</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L57)

RenderToTexture variant that ring-buffers every color attachment. Each frame it renders into one image set while exposing previous completed frames via `otherImageView` and [`previousFrameImageViews`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--pingpongrendertotexture--previousframeimageviews), so modules can sample feedback history without managing several RTT instances.

### FrameCadencedPingPongRenderToTexture { #pingpongrendertotexture-kt-framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FrameCadencedPingPongRenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">fromContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">framesPerPingPong</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RTTParameters</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PingPongRenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L661)

A [`PingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt-pingpongrendertotexture) that only advances the frame ring once every [`framesPerPingPong`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framesperpingpong) render calls. Between advances, `thisImageView` remains the latest completed texture and `otherImageView` remains the previous one, so downstream modules can crossfade from `other` to `this` with [`crossfade`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--crossfade).

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framesperpingpong"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">framesPerPingPong</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L671) | How many render calls one ring slot is held for: 1 advances every frame, 4 renders once and shows that result for four. Writing a value below 1 stores 1, and shortening the period also pulls [`framesSincePingPong`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framessincepingpong) back inside it, so the next advance is not stranded. |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framessincepingpong"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">framesSincePingPong</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L679) | Render calls since the last advance, counting 0 on the frame that advanced. It drives [`crossfade`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--crossfade) and [`framePhase`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framephase), and reaching [`framesPerPingPong`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framesperpingpong) less one is what makes the next call render. |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--pingpongcount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">pingPongCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L683) | How many times the ring has advanced, which is how many frames this target has actually rendered as against the render calls it was given. Zero until the first, which is why the first call always renders whatever the cadence says. |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framesuntilpingpong"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">framesUntilPingPong</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L687) | Render calls still to be held before the ring advances again: 0 means the next call renders. It is also 0 before the first advance, which is not waiting on the cadence. |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--crossfade"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">crossfade</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L694) | 0 immediately after a ping-pong render, 1 on the last held frame before the next one. Intended for `mix(other, this, crossfade)`. |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--framephase"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">framePhase</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L702) | Similar to [`crossfade`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--crossfade), but normalized by the whole cadence period and therefore stays below 1 before the next ping-pong. |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--frameimageviewthisindex"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">frameImageViewThisIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L705) |  |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--thisimageview"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">thisImageView</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasImageView</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L708) |  |
| <a id="pingpongrendertotexture-kt--framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture--otherimageview"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">otherImageView</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasImageView</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L710) |  |

## PointAccumulation.kt { #pointaccumulation-kt }

Accumulating points: GPU points plotted into a float image that fades a little every frame, so
they build up into dust, trails or a density picture. [`PointAccumulation`](graphics.md#pointaccumulation-kt-pointaccumulation) is the target;
[AccumulatedPoint](graphics.md#pointaccumulation-kt--pointaccumulation--plot) records are what it plots.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PointAccumulation.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PointAccumulation/)

### PointBlend { #pointaccumulation-kt-pointblend }

How points combine with what is already in a [`PointAccumulation`](graphics.md#pointaccumulation-kt-pointaccumulation).

Constants: `ADDITIVE`, `ALPHA`.

## RenderTarget.kt { #rendertarget-kt }

The render pass that draws a window's swapchain image: an ordered collection of modules, mesh
modules and other targets recorded into one frame.

Add passes with `+=` on a [`RenderTarget`](graphics.md#rendertarget-kt-rendertarget); a [`RendersAfter`](graphics.md#rendertarget-kt-rendersafter) pass is moved behind the target it
depends on before the list is recorded.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderTarget.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderTarget/)

## RenderToTexture.kt { #rendertotexture-kt }

Offscreen rendering: [`RenderToTexture`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture) draws modules into its own color (and optional depth)
images, which other modules then sample as textures.

A box beneath the renderer builds one with a configuration block over [`RTTParameters`](graphics.md#rendertotexture-kt-rttparameters) (size,
formats, attachment count, mip levels, clearing, depth), registers modules to draw into it, and
hands its image views to whatever samples the result. The same target can be blitted to the
window, read back to the CPU, or saved as a JPEG. [`PingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt-pingpongrendertotexture) and
[`MultiPingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#multipingpongrendertotexture-kt-multipingpongrendertotexture) build feedback and multi-pass chains from it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderToTexture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderToTexture/)

### RenderToTexture { #rendertotexture-kt-rendertotexture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">open</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">fromContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RTTParameters</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Target</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">HasImageView</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">HasImageViewArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">HasDefaultTextureSampler</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">PreparesSampledImages</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderToTexture/#L153)

An offscreen target holding one set of color attachments, any number of them, which its modules draw into and other modules sample as textures. Optionally a depth+stencil attachment as well, to depth-test against while rendering. The attachments are single-buffered, so reading last frame's output while writing this one is [`PingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt-pingpongrendertotexture)'s job rather than this class's.

| <a id="rendertotexture-kt--rendertotexture--colorimagehandles"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">colorImageHandles</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderToTexture/#L215) | The `VkImage` handle of each color attachment, external slots included; its size is the number of attachments, which every module registered here has to declare. |

## RollingCapture.kt { #rollingcapture-kt }

Reads a rendered image back to the CPU a strip at a time, so a full-frame capture never stalls a
frame.

[`RollingCapture`](graphics.md#rollingcapture-kt-rollingcapture) copies one horizontal strip per frame into a snapshot image, then copies the
finished snapshot into a CPU-visible staging buffer.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/)

### RollingCapture { #rollingcapture-kt-rollingcapture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingCapture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Image</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rowsPerFrame</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">16</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sourceLayout</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">VK&#95;IMAGE&#95;LAYOUT&#95;SHADER&#95;READ&#95;ONLY&#95;OPTIMAL</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">downsample</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/#L43)

Rolling capture that copies a horizontal strip from a source image into an internal snapshot image each frame. Once a full frame has been copied, you can copy the snapshot to a CPU-visible buffer (e.g., on a low-priority transfer queue) without stalling rendering.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--snapshotview"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">snapshotView</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/#L65) | A view of the snapshot image itself, so a pass can sample the partly-rebuilt frame on the GPU without waiting for a CPU readback. Expect to see the strip boundary: the rows above [`recordStrip`](graphics.md#rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--recordstrip)'s next row are from this sweep and the rows below are from the previous one. |
| <a id="rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--stagingbuffer"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stagingBuffer</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/#L79) | Host-visible, host-coherent buffer holding one whole captured frame, tightly packed at the capture's own size after `downsample`. [`copySnapshotToStaging`](graphics.md#rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--copysnapshottostaging) fills it; nothing here synchronises the read, so wait on that copy's fence before looking at the bytes. |
| <a id="rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--fullframeready"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">fullFrameReady</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/#L93) | True once the strips have covered the whole image and the snapshot is a complete frame. While it is true [`recordStrip`](graphics.md#rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--recordstrip) does nothing, so capture pauses rather than overwriting a frame nobody has taken; [`copySnapshotToStaging`](graphics.md#rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--copysnapshottostaging) clears it and the next strip starts a new sweep. |

Call this at the end of your frame on the graphics command buffer. |
| <a id="rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--copysnapshottostaging"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">copySnapshotToStaging</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">command</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CommandBuffer</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/#L216) | Copy the accumulated snapshot image to the staging buffer. Call on a transfer/graphics command buffer after checking [`fullFrameReady`](graphics.md#rollingcapture-kt--rollingcapture--fullframeready). |

## SideBySideStereoTarget.kt { #sidebysidestereotarget-kt }

Stereo rendering into one packed image: [`SideBySideStereoTarget`](graphics.md#sidebysidestereotarget-kt-sidebysidestereotarget) draws the scene once per eye
and lays the two views side by side, left eye on the left half.

With an [`OpenXRHmdTarget`](graphics.md#openxrhmdtarget-kt-openxrhmdtarget) attached, the per-eye view and projection matrices come from the
headset and the packed image can feed its swapchains; without one, an internal stereo camera
supplies them, so the same box code renders a stereo pair on a desktop window.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/SideBySideStereoTarget.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/SideBySideStereoTarget/)

**Used in:** [Field on Apple Vision Pro](../vision.md)

### StereoCamera { #sidebysidestereotarget-kt-stereocamera }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StereoCamera</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">base</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Camera</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Camera</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/SideBySideStereoTarget/#L684)

Minimal stereo camera: offsets along the right vector by +/-IPD/2, converges on a focus point, and supports asymmetric frustum offsets through the base projection.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="sidebysidestereotarget-kt--stereocamera--ipd"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ipd</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/SideBySideStereoTarget/#L689) | Interpupillary distance in world units, split half to each side of `base` along its right vector. The default 0.064 is the usual adult average in metres. |
| <a id="sidebysidestereotarget-kt--stereocamera--convergencedistance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">convergenceDistance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/SideBySideStereoTarget/#L694) | Distance multiplier for the stereo convergence point, measured from the base camera toward its target along the forward vector. |
| <a id="sidebysidestereotarget-kt--stereocamera--asymmetricfrustumoffset"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">asymmetricFrustumOffset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/SideBySideStereoTarget/#L702) | Shifts each eye's principal point instead of toeing its view in: the left eye gets `-asymmetricFrustumOffset` and the right `+asymmetricFrustumOffset` as the base projection's `ox`, so the units are half-widths of what that projection frames at its match depth. ## StereoPoseSource.kt { #stereoposesource-kt }

The interface for a stereo head pose that arrives from somewhere other than OpenXR, such as a
remote headset.

A [`StereoPoseSource`](graphics.md#stereoposesource-kt-stereoposesource) is latched once per frame so both eyes render from the same pose, and it
reports which frame that pose belongs to.

## 16bits.kt { #16bits-kt }

Half-precision (binary16) conversion and packing for data headed to GPU buffers.

[`floatToHalfBits`](graphics.md#16bits-kt--floattohalfbits) and [`halfBitsToFloat`](graphics.md#16bits-kt--halfbitstofloat) convert single values, [`packHalf1x16`](graphics.md#16bits-kt--packhalf1x16) and [`packHalf2x16`](graphics.md#16bits-kt--packhalf2x16) pack them as GLSL's `packHalf2x16` does, and the `.half` views ([`Vec2h`](graphics.md#16bits-kt-vec2h), [`Vec3h`](graphics.md#16bits-kt-vec3h), [`Vec4h`](graphics.md#16bits-kt-vec4h)) mark a Field vector for 16-bit storage.

A two-component vector marked for 16-bit storage, holding the full-precision `Vector2f` until something writes it out.

### Vec3h { #16bits-kt-vec3h }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Vec3h</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">v</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector3f</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/16bits/#L28)

Three components marked for 16-bit storage. The packed form is two `uint`s — `x` and `y` in the first, `z` in the low half of the second — so it costs the same eight bytes a `uvec2` does.

### Vec4h { #16bits-kt-vec4h }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Vec4h</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">v</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector4f</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/16bits/#L34)

Four components marked for 16-bit storage, packed into two `uint`s and read back in the shader as a `uvec2`: eight bytes where a `vec4` takes sixteen, at enough precision for a colour.

## AutoDisposer.kt { #autodisposer-kt }

Releases Vulkan handles when the Kotlin object that owned them is garbage collected.

A resource calls [`AutoDisposer.register`](graphics.md#autodisposer-kt--autodisposer--register) with a cleanup lambda and keeps the returned
[`AutoDisposer.Token`](graphics.md#autodisposer-kt--autodisposer--token). When the object has been collected, the renderer's frame loop calls
[`AutoDisposer.drain`](graphics.md#autodisposer-kt--autodisposer--drain) and queues the cleanup on its retirement queue. Explicit cleanup calls
`AutoDisposer.Token.disable` first, so a resource is released at most once whichever path gets
there first. Tests are in `AutoDisposerTest`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/AutoDisposer.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/AutoDisposer/)

GC-driven disposal, with optional device ownership for deterministic shutdown. Cleanup actions must capture handles, not the registered object itself.

## Camera.kt { #camera-kt }

The Vulkan renderer's look-at camera: a position, a target and an up vector, with a [`SuperProjection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-superprojection) for its projection.

[`Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera) supplies the model-view matrix as a uniform and moves in world or camera-local terms: dolly, pan, yaw, pitch, roll, and rotation around either the camera position or the target. [`OrbitControls`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt-orbitcontrols) drives it from the mouse, and `CameraPose.kt` converts it to and from a rigid pose.

## CameraPose.kt { #camerapose-kt }

Rigid camera poses for blending between viewpoints: [`CameraPose`](graphics.md#camerapose-kt-camerapose) stores a [`Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera)'s placement as a dual quaternion plus a focus distance.

[`pose`](graphics.md#camerapose-kt--pose) reads one from a camera and [`applyPose`](graphics.md#camerapose-kt--applypose) writes it back. [`sclerpTo`](graphics.md#camerapose-kt--sclerpto) moves a camera toward a target pose by screw interpolation and [`nlerpTo`](graphics.md#camerapose-kt--nlerpto) by normalised linear interpolation.

## DeferredCleanup.kt { #deferredcleanup-kt }

Releases a renderer's deferred GPU resources at shutdown, when no later frame will come to age
them out.

While a renderer is running, a resource retired by one frame waits in a queue until the frames
that might still be reading it have finished. Shutdown removes that guarantee, so [`Renderer`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-renderer)
drains the queues by hand: once the present queue, the graph queue and the device are idle, and
then again after releasing the resources a document still held, because releasing those enqueues
more work of its own.

Each batch is cleared before it is invoked, so a destructor may enqueue dependent work, and a
destructor that throws does not strand the resources queued behind it. Failures are collected and
handed back for the owner to report once the rest of its teardown is done, which is why a broken
release shows up as one exception with the others suppressed on it rather than as a half-finished
shutdown.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/DeferredCleanup.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/DeferredCleanup/)

## FieldProbe.kt { #fieldprobe-kt }

Samples values out of a running shader into a GPU buffer and shows them in a box's output as a histogram and summary statistics.

A shader includes `fieldProbe` and writes scalar or vector samples into a buffer bound at
[`FIELD_PROBE_DEFAULT_BINDING`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--field-probe-default-binding); [`ShaderFieldProbe`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt-shaderfieldprobe) reads that buffer back off the render thread,
builds a [`FieldProbeSnapshot`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt-fieldprobesnapshot) (counts of NaN, infinite and non-zero samples, ranges, summaries)
and, with [`ShaderFieldProbe.display`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--shaderfieldprobe--display), publishes it to an output channel at most
[`ShaderFieldProbe.maxDisplayHz`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--shaderfieldprobe--maxdisplayhz) times a second. [`ShaderFieldProbe.ordinalRange`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--shaderfieldprobe--ordinalrange) limits which
invocations record, and [`ShaderFieldProbe.onSnapshot`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--shaderfieldprobe--onsnapshot) hands each snapshot to box code.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/)

| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--field-probe-default-set"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">FIELD&#95;PROBE&#95;DEFAULT&#95;SET</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L86) | Default descriptor set for the probe buffer, 0. |

### FieldProbeSnapshot { #fieldprobe-kt-fieldprobesnapshot }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FieldProbeSnapshot</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">dimensions</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">invocationCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">acceptedCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">finiteCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sampleCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nanCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">infCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nonZeroCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">typeMismatchCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">exactMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">exactMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec4</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L156)

One frame's worth of probe data: how many times the shader called `fieldProbe`, what it was holding, and a bounded sample of the values themselves.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">dimensions</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many components each recorded value had: 1 for a scalar, 2, 3 or 4 for a vector, and 0 if nothing was recorded. The first call of a frame fixes this, and later calls of a different width are counted as [`typeMismatchCount`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--typemismatchcount) instead. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--invocationcount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">invocationCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many times the shader called `fieldProbe` while the probe was enabled, before any filtering: the denominator for how much of the work was looked at. Each call's position in this count is its ordinal. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--acceptedcount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">acceptedCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many of those calls got past the ordinal range and the width check, and so contributed to everything below. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--finitecount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">finiteCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many accepted values were finite in every component. Also the index space the reservoir fills, so `min(finiteCount, capacity)` is [`sampleCount`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--samplecount). |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--samplecount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sampleCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many values are actually in [`samples`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--samples): [`finiteCount`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--finitecount) capped at the configured capacity. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--nancount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nanCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many accepted values had a NaN component. These are counted and dropped, so they do not reach the ranges or the samples; [`anyNaN`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--anynan) is the quick test. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--infcount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">infCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many accepted values had an infinite component — counted and dropped like the NaNs, and checked after them, so a value that is both is counted only as NaN. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--nonzerocount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nonZeroCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many finite values had at least one non-zero component, counting only the components [`dimensions`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions) says are real. A probe whose output should not be zero and whose count here is zero has found something. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--typemismatchcount"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">typeMismatchCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How many in-range calls were rejected for recording a different number of components than the first call of the frame did. Normally zero; non-zero means two probes of different widths are sharing one buffer, and only the first width is being measured. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--exactmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">exactMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The true minimum of each component over every accepted finite value, one entry per recorded component. Computed with integer atomics across the whole frame, so these are not limited to the sampled values. When nothing finite was recorded every entry is NaN, and there is one of them. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--exactmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">exactMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">DoubleArray</span></code> | The true maximum of each component, on the same terms as [`exactMin`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--exactmin). |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--samples"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec4</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The retained values, always as `Vec4` whatever [`dimensions`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions) is, with the unused components zero. Up to the capacity they are every finite value in order; past it the shader replaces a hashed slot, which keeps the retained set spread across the frame rather than stopping at the first thousand. Read them through [`scalarValues`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--scalarvalues) and the vector forms, which narrow them to the recorded width. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--anynan"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">anyNaN</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L280) | Whether any accepted value had a NaN component this frame. The first thing to check when a render goes black. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--anyinf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">anyInf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L284) | Whether any accepted value had an infinite component this frame. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--anynonzero"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">anyNonZero</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L289) | Whether any finite value was not all zeros: the test for "did this code path run and produce anything". |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--scalarvalues"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">scalarValues</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L294) | The retained values as plain numbers, or `null` if this frame recorded vectors rather than scalars. Checking for `null` is how you find out what the shader was probing. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--vec2values"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">vec2Values</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L297) | The retained values as two-component vectors, or `null` if [`dimensions`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions) is not 2. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--vec3values"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">vec3Values</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L300) | The retained values as three-component vectors, or `null` if [`dimensions`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions) is not 3. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--vec4values"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">vec4Values</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Vec4</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L304) | The retained values as four-component vectors, or `null` if [`dimensions`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions) is not 4. Note that [`samples`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--samples) is `Vec4` whatever the width, while this is `null` unless the width really was 4. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--scalarsummary"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">scalarSummary</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SummaryStats</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L309) | Count, mean, spread and quartiles over the retained scalar values, or `null` if this frame was not scalar. Computed from the sample rather than from every call, so compare it against [`exactMin`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--exactmin) and [`exactMax`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--exactmax) rather than treating it as the whole story. |
| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--vec2summary"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">vec2Summary</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2SummaryStats</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L313) | Per-component summary statistics over the retained two-component values, or `null` if [`dimensions`](graphics.md#fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--dimensions) is not 2. |

| <a id="fieldprobe-kt--fieldprobesnapshot--summaryhtml"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">summaryHtml</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">previous</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FieldProbeSnapshot</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">widthPx</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">520</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">chartHeightPx</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">120</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">decimals</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">background</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;#000000&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">textColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;#0af&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">accentColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;#0af&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldProbe/#L353) | Renders this snapshot as the HTML card a probe shows in a box's output: the counts, then a histogram and summary for a scalar frame, or a per-component table and a vector-length histogram for a vector one. |

## FieldStats.kt { #fieldstats-kt }

Computes streaming statistics of shader values on the GPU and reads the results back to box code.

[`ShaderFieldStats`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt-shaderfieldstats) owns a partial buffer and a result buffer (default bindings
[`FIELD_STATS_DEFAULT_PARTIAL_BINDING`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt--field-stats-default-partial-binding) and [`FIELD_STATS_DEFAULT_RESULT_BINDING`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt--field-stats-default-result-binding)) for a shader
that includes `fieldStats`. Each channel reduces to a [`FieldScalarStatsSnapshot`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt-fieldscalarstatssnapshot), whose
[`FieldScalarStatsSnapshot.quantile`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt--fieldscalarstatssnapshot--quantile) and [`FieldScalarStatsSnapshot.cdf`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt--fieldscalarstatssnapshot--cdf) read a fixed-size
centroid sketch; [`ShaderFieldStats.scalar`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt--shaderfieldstats--scalar) and [`ShaderFieldStats.state`](graphics.md#fieldstats-kt--shaderfieldstats--state) give per-channel and
per-slot handles with `read()` and `latest()`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldStats.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/FieldStats/)

The per-frame blend is `1 - 2^(-1/halfLife)`, so larger is slower; the shader side floors it just above zero. |

A slot starts uninitialised and takes its first frame's statistic whole rather than blending up from zero, and a slot whose mode, channel, quantile or half-life changes restarts the same way, so a reconfigured slot does not drift from its old value to its new one. |

## FramePresentationLog.kt { #framepresentationlog-kt }

A diagnostic log of swapchain presentation timing, written to a file while enabled.

[`FramePresentationLog`](graphics.md#framepresentationlog-kt-framepresentationlog) records when each present call was made and returned, and when the presentation or scanout of that image was observed; [`FramePresentationLog.mark`](graphics.md#framepresentationlog-kt--framepresentationlog--mark) adds a labelled line to the same log.

## GpuNeighbourGrid.kt { #gpuneighbourgrid-kt }

A uniform spatial grid over a particle buffer, rebuilt on the GPU each frame with [`GpuRadixSort`](graphics.md#gpuradixsort-kt-gpuradixsort), so a compute shader can find a particle's neighbours by visiting nearby cells.

## GpuProbe.kt { #gpuprobe-kt }

Runs a compute shader against fixture buffers, checks that it ran, and compares its read-back output with stated bounds.

[`GpuProbe`](graphics.md#gpuprobe-kt-gpuprobe) is the facility; a probe whose shader never produced output throws
[`GpuProbeNeverLanded`](graphics.md#gpuprobe-kt-gpuprobeneverlanded).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/GpuProbe.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/GpuProbe/)

## GpuRadixSort.kt { #gpuradixsort-kt }

A stable GPU radix sort of `uint` keys in storage buffers, with an optional `uint` payload carried along.

[`GpuRadixSort`](graphics.md#gpuradixsort-kt-gpuradixsort) owns its scratch buffers and compute shaders. [`asFrameBufferGroup`](graphics.md#gpuradixsort-kt--asframebuffergroup) wraps a single [`VulkanBuffer`](graphics.md#vulkanbuffer-kt-vulkanbuffer) so it can be passed where a per-frame buffer group is expected.

## ImageReducer.kt { #imagereducer-kt }

Reduces an image to global summary statistics on the GPU in two compute passes.

[`ImageReducer`](graphics.md#imagereducer-kt-imagereducer) reads the source as a sampled texture, so the image needs the sampled usage bit and its layout is left alone; results come back through [`ImageReducer.readResults`](graphics.md#imagereducer-kt--imagereducer--readresults).

## KeyCamera.kt { #keycamera-kt }

Keyboard camera controls for a Vulkan window.

[`KeyCamera`](graphics.md#keycamera-kt-keycamera) registers a poll callback on the renderer that moves a [`Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera) from held keys; [`keyCamera`](graphics.md#keycamera-kt--keycamera) and [`KeyCameraDelegateProvider`](graphics.md#keycamera-kt-keycameradelegateprovider) create one named after the property it is assigned to, so re-running a box replaces its controls rather than adding more.

## MouseEvents.kt { #mouseevents-kt }

Mouse input from a Vulkan renderer's window, delivered to named callbacks.

[`MouseEvents`](graphics.md#mouseevents-kt-mouseevents) registers handlers for down, up, move, drag and scroll, keyed by a name so that re-running a box replaces its handler rather than adding another. Each handler receives a [`MouseEvent`](graphics.md#mouseevents-kt-mouseevent) with position, delta, scroll, buttons held, and the window size.

## Options.kt { #options-kt }

Global switches for the Vulkan renderer, mostly read from system properties at startup, and the code that locates the Vulkan loader and driver.

[`Options`](graphics.md#options-kt-options) holds the platform flags, profiling and frame-presentation logging toggles, debug
naming and labels, and VR. On macOS, [`Options.doVulkanSDK`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--dovulkansdk) uses the loader named by
`AFIELD_VULKAN_LIBRARY`, else `VULKAN_SDK`, else the newest `~/VulkanSDK` version, falls back to
LWJGL's bundled MoltenVK when none exists, and pins the driver chosen by [`Options.macVulkanDriver`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--macvulkandriver-2).

An SDK whose directory names no version (a hand-set `VULKAN_SDK`) is taken at its word. |

A path that does not exist is ignored, and setting it after Vulkan has loaded changes nothing. |

| <a id="options-kt--options--framepresentationlogpath"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">framePresentationLogPath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L172) | Where to write that log. `afield.four.framePresentationLogPath` or `AFIELD_FOUR_FRAME_PRESENTATION_LOG_PATH`; null or blank lets `FramePresentationLog` choose a timestamped path and report it. |

Off, each acquire first waits for the *previous* present, so a frame's presentation is observed a frame late; on, every present is waited for as soon as it is made, which dates it to the frame it belongs to and costs throughput. `afield.four.framePresentationLogWaitAfterPresent` or `AFIELD_FOUR_FRAME_PRESENTATION_LOG_WAIT_AFTER_PRESENT`. |

Default 120, floored at 1; 1 costs a write per line and is what to use when the run may end in a crash. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--framepresentationlogpresentwaittimeoutns"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">framePresentationLogPresentWaitTimeoutNs</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L197) | How long `vkWaitForPresentKHR` is given, in nanoseconds. Default 50 ms, floored at 1 ns; a wait that times out warns and the frame goes on, so this bounds a stalled compositor rather than tuning anything. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--presenttimingqueuesize"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">presentTimingQueueSize</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L206) | How many past-presentation-timing slots the swapchain reserves for `VK_EXT_present_timing`. | <a id="options-kt--options--logshadercsource"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">logShadercSource</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L215) | Log the line-numbered GLSL handed to shaderc, on the `debug,graphics` channel, for every stage compiled. | <a id="options-kt--options--computeonceperframe"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">computeOncePerFrame</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L225) | Record the compute pass once per frame rather than once per window. On by default: a simulation stepped per window advances two or three times a frame when the same document has several windows open on it. `afield.four.computeOncePerFrame` or `AFIELD_FOUR_COMPUTE_ONCE_PER_FRAME`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--unifiedimagelayouts"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">unifiedImageLayouts</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L240) | Ask for `VK_KHR_unified_image_layouts` where the device offers it, which lets every layout but `UNDEFINED`, `PREINITIALIZED` and `PRESENT_SRC` go to Vulkan as `GENERAL` (`ImageLayouts`). On by default on macOS only, where the GPU sweep has run with it; elsewhere it is `afield.four.unifiedLayouts` or `AFIELD_FOUR_UNIFIED_LAYOUTS=true`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--onetimesubmitframes"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">oneTimeSubmitFrames</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L250) | Record the renderer's per-frame command buffers with `ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`, telling the driver each is submitted once and can be discarded after. On by default, and a switch rather than a constant so the gain can be measured on a driver without a rebuild. `afield.four.oneTimeSubmit` or `AFIELD_FOUR_ONE_TIME_SUBMIT`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--secondarygraphicscommandbuffers"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">secondaryGraphicsCommandBuffers</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L261) | Record a window's graphics work into secondary command buffers, so several can be recorded in parallel. Asked for by default, and used only where `Device.supportsMaintenance7` also holds, so on a device without that extension this reads true and nothing changes. `afield.four.secondaryGraphicsCommandBuffers` or `AFIELD_FOUR_SECONDARY_GRAPHICS_COMMAND_BUFFERS`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--capturecompatibility"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">captureCompatibility</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L275) | Run as a GPU capture tool expects: it clears [`validate`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--validate), [`dumpToolingInfo`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--dumptoolinginfo), [`debugObjectNames`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--debugobjectnames), [`debugLabels`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--debuglabels) and [`shaderDebugPrintf`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--shaderdebugprintf), every one of which either injects a layer of its own or annotates the stream a capture is trying to read. `afield.four.captureCompatibility` or `AFIELD_FOUR_CAPTURE_COMPAT`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--dumptoolinginfo"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dumpToolingInfo</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L286) | Report the tooling layers attached to the device, which answers "is a capture tool in this stream". Off by default, because the call that asks — `vkGetPhysicalDeviceToolPropertiesEXT` — runs inside whatever layer injected itself, and under Nsight that has taken the JVM down at startup. `afield.four.dumpToolingInfo` or `AFIELD_FOUR_DUMP_TOOLING_INFO`, and [`captureCompatibility`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--capturecompatibility) holds it off. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--debugobjectnames"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">debugObjectNames</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L296) | Attach names to Vulkan handles, so a validation message or a RenderDoc capture says which buffer rather than which address. On by default, and inert unless [`validate`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--validate) is on and the driver exposes `VK_EXT_debug_utils`. `afield.four.debugObjectNames` or `AFIELD_FOUR_DEBUG_OBJECT_NAMES`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--debuglabels"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">debugLabels</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L305) | Bracket regions of a command buffer with labels, which is what gives a frame debugger its nesting. Same conditions as [`debugObjectNames`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--debugobjectnames), and additionally skipped on macOS. `afield.four.debugLabels` or `AFIELD_FOUR_DEBUG_LABELS`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--enablevr"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enableVR</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L318) | Bring up OpenXR alongside Vulkan: the instance and device ask for the runtime's required extensions, the renderer creates an XR session, and the swapchain picks a format the runtime will take. Off by default and set from the user's preferences at startup, so it is read before the instance exists and changing it afterwards does not reach one. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--dovulkansdk"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">doVulkanSDK</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L329) | Choose the Vulkan loader and driver. Must run before LWJGL first loads Vulkan, after which `VULKAN_LIBRARY_NAME` is ignored. `Window` and `Instance` call it themselves, because an entrypoint that does not silently gets LWJGL's bundled MoltenVK: no loader, no validation layers, no KosmicKrisp. Repeat calls do nothing. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--defaultdepthformat"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">defaultDepthFormat</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L431) | The depth format new depth attachments are created with. `D32_SFLOAT` until [`chooseDefaultDepthFormat`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--choosedefaultdepthformat) has asked a physical device, after which it is the first of `D32_SFLOAT`, `D16_UNORM`, `D24_UNORM_S8_UINT`, `D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT` that device can use as a depth attachment — unless `afield.four.depthFormat` or `AFIELD_FOUR_DEPTH_FORMAT` named one (`D16`, `D32`, `D24S8`, `D32S8`), which pins it with no support check at all. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--choosedefaultdepthformat"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">chooseDefaultDepthFormat</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">physicalDevice</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VkPhysicalDevice</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L433) |  |
| <a id="options-kt--options--depthhasstencil"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">depthHasStencil</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">format</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L462) |  |
| <a id="options-kt--options--depthaspectmask"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">depthAspectMask</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">format</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L465) |  |
| <a id="options-kt--options--depthformatname"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">depthFormatName</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">format</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L469) |  |
| <a id="options-kt--options--validateoverride"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">validateOverride</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L493) | What `afield.validate` or `AFIELD_VALIDATE` asked for, or null when neither is set to a strict `true` or `false`. Kept apart from [`validate`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--validate) so that "nobody said" is distinguishable from "someone said no": the server takes the user's preference only in the null case, so a command-line answer outranks the preference without having to be re-stated. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--validate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">validate</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L506) | Ask the instance for `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`. On in a bare entrypoint, and under the server whatever [`validateOverride`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--validateoverride) says, or the user's preference when it says nothing; [`captureCompatibility`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--capturecompatibility) clears it either way. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--shaderdebugprintf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">shaderDebugPrintf</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L514) | Enable `debugPrintfEXT` in shaders without turning all of [`validate`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--validate) on, since the printf plumbing rides on the same validation layer. Off by default; with neither this nor [`validate`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--validate) on, a shader's `printf` compiles and prints nothing, and the compiler warns once that it will. `afield.four.shaderDebugPrintf` or `AFIELD_FOUR_SHADER_DEBUG_PRINTF`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--preferreddevice"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">preferredDevice</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L526) | Pick a physical device by its exact reported name rather than by the default rule. Null, and nothing sets it from the environment, so this is for code that has read the device names and wants one of them. A name that matches nothing, or matches a device missing a required extension, is not an error: selection falls through to the default, which on macOS is the device belonging to the driver [`resolvedMacVulkanDriver`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--resolvedmacvulkandriver) names and elsewhere the first that qualifies. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--enableraytracing"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enableRayTracing</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L529) | Ask the device for the ray-tracing pipeline and acceleration-structure extensions. On, and skipped on a device that does not offer them, so the cost of leaving it on is a feature query. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--requestedimages"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">requestedImages</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L538) | How many swapchain images to ask for, 3 by default. It is an upper bound rather than a count: the swapchain clamps the request to the surface's maximum and then raises it to the surface's minimum, and a surface that reports *no* maximum drops the request altogether and gives its minimum, which is usually 2. A window that will not triple-buffer is generally that, rather than a driver refusing. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--vsync"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">vsync</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L547) | Prefer a present mode that waits for vertical blank. On, which on macOS is FIFO, on Windows mailbox and on Linux relaxed FIFO; off puts immediate first, which tears and is what a frame-rate measurement wants. [`enableVR`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--enablevr) overrides it either way, because the desktop window is then a mirror on the same loop as `xrWaitFrame` and a blocking desktop present would cap the headset at the monitor's rate. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--maxframerate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxFrameRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L556) | Upper bound on renderer frames per second; 0 (the default) leaves the loop uncapped. A window the compositor is not showing is not throttled by [`vsync`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--vsync) and can run at thousands of frames a second, so anything measured per frame (motion vectors, frame-to-frame displacement) shrinks towards zero. A capture that shows per-frame motion sets this, in its renderer box or through `AFIELD_MAX_FRAME_RATE`. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--fov"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">fov</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L581) | Default vertical field of view, in **radians** — [`Projection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-projection) and [`SuperProjection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-superprojection) hand it straight to `setPerspective(fovy, …)` and `tan(fov / 2)` respectively. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--znear"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">zNear</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L588) | Default near clip distance, in world units, which every [`Projection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-projection) and [`SuperProjection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-superprojection) starts from. 0.001 is close enough that a camera a metre from its subject does not clip it, and near enough zero to spend most of the depth buffer's precision on the first few units; push it out if depth fighting matters more than close geometry. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--zfar"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">zFar</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L591) | Default far clip distance, in world units. 1000, with [`zNear`](graphics.md#options-kt--options--znear) giving the ratio the depth buffer's precision follows from. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--openxrclearcolor"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">openXRClearColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatArray</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L594) | The colour the OpenXR target clears each eye to, as RGBA. Opaque black. The desktop window has its own clear colour and does not read this. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--enablehdr"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enableHDR</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L605) | Prefer an HDR surface format — scRGB or HDR10 — over the default 8-bit sRGB, which needs `VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace` on the instance and a display advertising an HDR colorspace. Where either is missing the swapchain is sRGB and nothing says so, so check the chosen surface format rather than this flag. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--openxrdebuginput"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">openXRDebugInput</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L608) | Print what the OpenXR runtime bound: interaction profiles and the sources behind each action. On, since a controller doing nothing is usually a profile that did not bind. |
| <a id="options-kt--options--openxrwaitforgpubeforerelease"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">openXRWaitForGpuBeforeRelease</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/Options/#L619) | Wait for the GPU to finish rendering into an XR swapchain image before releasing it. Off: the frame is submitted and released at once, which is what most runtimes expect and is much the faster of the two, but it leaves the runtime's own synchronisation to be relied on. |

## OrbitControls.kt { #orbitcontrols-kt }

Mouse orbit controls for a [`Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera) in a Vulkan window: rotate, pan and dolly around the camera's target, after Three.js's OrbitControls.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/)

Mouse-driven orbit controls inspired by Three.js OrbitControls.

| Declaration | Summary |

| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--renderer"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span></code> | The renderer whose window supplies the mouse events, the key state for the drag modifiers and the poll loop that damping runs in. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--camera"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">camera</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Camera</span></code> | The camera these controls move. Its `at`, `target` and `up` are written on every [`update`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--update). |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--name"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The name the mouse handlers and the poll-loop entry are registered under, so a second set of controls on the same window does not displace the first. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--mouse"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">mouse</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MouseEvents</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L36) | The mouse stream these controls listen on: the window's own [`MouseEvents`](graphics.md#mouseevents-kt-mouseevents) when the constructor was given one, otherwise a private stream named `<name>__mouse__`. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--enabled"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enabled</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L39) | Whether drags and scrolls move the camera at all. While false the handlers return early and damping stops advancing, so the camera holds its pose. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--enablerotate"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enableRotate</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L42) | Whether a plain left-drag orbits the camera around the camera's target. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--enablepan"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enablePan</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L45) | Whether a right-drag, or shift and left-drag, slides camera and target together. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--enablezoom"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enableZoom</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L48) | Whether the scroll wheel, a middle-drag and ctrl (or alt) with a left-drag change the distance to the target. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--rotatespeed"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">rotateSpeed</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L51) | Radians of orbit per pixel dragged, as a multiple of a full turn across the window: at 1.0, dragging the window's own height turns 360° about either axis. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--zoomspeed"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">zoomSpeed</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L54) | How sharply scrolling and dollying change the distance to the target: an event of `d` units multiplies it by `0.95` raised to `zoomSpeed * d / 100`, inwards or outwards according to the sign. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--panspeed"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">panSpeed</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L57) | Pan distance per pixel dragged, as a multiple of what the camera can see: at 1.0, dragging the window's own height moves the target by the full visible height at the target's distance, so the scene keeps pace with the pointer. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--enabledamping"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">enableDamping</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L65) | Whether a drag or scroll leaves momentum behind. While it is set, [`update`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--update) keeps being called from the window's poll loop after the mouse stops, each call applying and then shrinking what is left, until the pending angles are under a millionth of a radian and the pending pan under a thousandth of a world unit. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--dampingfactor"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dampingFactor</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L68) | The fraction of the pending orbit, pan and zoom that each damped [`update`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--update) discards: 0.1 keeps nine tenths of the momentum per frame, 1.0 spends it all in one frame, and 0.0 never settles. Read only while [`enableDamping`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--enabledamping) is set. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--mindistance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">minDistance</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L71) | The closest the camera may come to its target; the distance is clamped into this range by every [`update`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--update), not only by the drag that crossed it. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--maxdistance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxDistance</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L74) | The farthest the camera may sit from its target, infinite by default; clamped like [`minDistance`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--mindistance). |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--minpolarangle"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">minPolarAngle</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L77) | The smallest angle, in radians, between [`upAxis`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--upaxis) and the direction from target to camera: 0 is directly overhead, and the camera is held a millionth of a radian inside the limit so the pole itself stays unreachable. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--maxpolarangle"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxPolarAngle</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L80) | The largest such angle, `PI` (directly underneath) by default; held just inside the limit like [`minPolarAngle`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--minpolarangle), which is what keeps the picture from flipping over at the pole. |
| <a id="orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--screenspacepanning"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">screenSpacePanning</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/util/OrbitControls/#L87) | Which plane a pan moves the target in. Set, the drag moves it in the plane of the screen, along the camera's own up; clear, it moves in the plane that [`upAxis`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--upaxis) is normal to, so a vertical drag travels along the ground rather than lifting the target off it. |

Every [`update`](graphics.md#orbitcontrols-kt--orbitcontrols--update) writes it back into the camera, so the horizon stays level however far the orbit has travelled. |

## Projection.kt { #projection-kt }

Projection matrices for the Vulkan renderer: a plain perspective [`Projection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-projection) and a [`SuperProjection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-superprojection) that blends perspective into orthographic.

[`SuperProjection`](graphics.md#projection-kt-superprojection) is what [`Camera`](graphics.md#camera-kt-camera) uses. Its `orthoness` runs from 0 (perspective) to 1 (orthographic) along a matrix-log path, with `matchDepth` (or the camera's distance to its target) as the depth where the two footprints agree, and `ox`/`oy` shifting the principal point.

The remaining functions are the matrix tools behind that blend: [`matrix4fToSimple`](graphics.md#projection-kt--matrix4ftosimple) and [`simpleToMatrix4f`](graphics.md#projection-kt--simpletomatrix4f) convert to EJML, [`expmEigen`](graphics.md#projection-kt--expmeigen) and [`logmEigen`](graphics.md#projection-kt--logmeigen) take the matrix exponential and logarithm, [`lieInterpolateProjectionEJML`](graphics.md#projection-kt--lieinterpolateprojectionejml) interpolates two projections, and [`renormDepth01`](graphics.md#projection-kt--renormdepth01) and [`renormVerticalFovAtDepth`](graphics.md#projection-kt--renormverticalfovatdepth) rescale a matrix's depth range and its field of view at a chosen depth.

## VulkanProbe.kt { #vulkanprobe-kt }

Reports what Vulkan this machine offers: loader, instance, devices, validation layers, the SDK and, on macOS, the KosmicKrisp driver.

[`VulkanProbe`](graphics.md#vulkanprobe-kt-vulkanprobe) runs the check in a child JVM and returns a [`VulkanStatus`](graphics.md#vulkanprobe-kt-vulkanstatus), which the Vulkan panel on `/welcome` shows along with install steps for the current OS. [`VulkanDeviceInfo`](graphics.md#vulkanprobe-kt-vulkandeviceinfo) describes one physical device.
